capabilities.name: Three-layer module topology and dual discovery
capabilities.behavior: Three layers. (1) Platform = `:app` — owns PluginRegistry, renderers, safety-limit enforcement, credential storage. Plugins never import from `:app`. (2) Plugin API = `:pump-driver-api` at `plugins/pump-driver-api/` — all interfaces, capability contracts, event types, declarative UI descriptors, domain models. Both platform and plugins depend on it. (3) Plugins — `:tandem-pump-driver` (`plugins/shipped/tandem/`), `:medtronic-pump-driver` (`plugins/shipped/medtronic/`), plus the in-`:app` Nightscout source, plus runtime JARs. settings.gradle.kts maps `:pump-driver-api`→plugins/pump-driver-api, `:tandem-pump-driver`→plugins/shipped/tandem, `:medtronic-pump-driver`→plugins/shipped/medtronic. Dual discovery: compile-time plugins arrive as a Hilt `Set<PluginFactory>` multibinding (`@Binds @IntoSet`); runtime plugins are loaded from `filesDir/plugins/*.jar` via DexClassLoader. ProGuard keeps (app/proguard-rules.pro lines 39-42): `-keep class com.glycemicgpt.mobile.domain.plugin.** { *; }`, `...domain.pump.** { *; }`, `...domain.model.** { *; }` — required because capability lookup is by KClass.
edge_cases: The Nightscout plugin lives in `:app` (not a standalone module) precisely because it needs `:app`'s Retrofit API + Room + WorkManager wiring, which a plugin module cannot depend on.
Runtime plugins are explicitly NOT compiled into official builds (CONTRIBUTING.md); they are an 'advanced contribution path'.

capabilities.name: Plugin interface and lifecycle contract
capabilities.behavior:
`interface Plugin` (pump-driver-api/domain/plugin/Plugin.kt): `val metadata: PluginMetadata`, `val capabilities: Set<PluginCapability>`, `fun initialize(context: PluginContext)`, `fun shutdown()`, `fun onActivated()`, `fun onDeactivated()`, `fun settingsDescriptor(): PluginSettingsDescriptor`, `fun observeDashboardCards(): Flow<List<DashboardCardDescriptor>>`, `fun <T : PluginCapabilityInterface> getCapability(type: KClass<T>): T?`, plus two defaulted members: `fun observeDetailScreen(cardId: String): Flow<DetailScreenDescriptor>? = null` and `fun onDetailAction(cardId: String, actionKey: String) {}`.

Lifecycle timing as implemented by PluginRegistry:
- `initialize(ctx)` — called once immediately after `factory.create(ctx)`, inside registry `initialize()` (compile-time) or `installRuntimePlugin`/`discoverRuntimePlugins` (runtime). Same PluginContext instance is passed to both create() and initialize().
- `onActivated()` — on user activation and on restore-from-preferences at startup.
- `onDeactivated()` — on user deactivation, on eviction by a conflicting single-instance plugin, and during runtime-plugin removal.
- `shutdown()` — ONLY called from `removeRuntimePlugin`. Compile-time plugins are never shut down by the registry (documented: 'plugins are garbage collected').

Error handling, exactly as coded:
- create()/initialize() throws → caught, `Timber.e`, plugin skipped entirely (absent from availablePlugins), and its settings store entry is removed from `pluginSettingsStores`.
- onActivated() throws → `Timber.e`, `Result.failure(e)` returned, plugin NOT added to activePlugins, preferences NOT written.
- onDeactivated() throws → caught + logged, deactivation continues; plugin is removed from activePlugins regardless (it is `remove()`d before the call).
- shutdown() throws during removeRuntimePlugin → caught + logged, cleanup continues.

Threading: activate/deactivate/install/remove/refreshSafetyLimits are all wrapped in `synchronized(activationLock)` (a plain `Any()`), so lifecycle callbacks for a given plugin are serialized. Capability methods may be invoked from arbitrary background dispatchers; `observeDashboardCards()`/`settingsDescriptor()` may be called from the UI thread.

Convenience extension functions on Plugin: `asGlucoseSource()`, `asInsulinSource()`, `asPumpStatus()`, `asBgmSource()`, `asCalibrationTarget()`, `asBolusCategoryProvider()` — each is `getCapability(X::class)`.
edge_cases: Registry deliberately activates the NEW plugin before deactivating the conflicting OLD one, so a single-instance capability slot is never momentarily empty.

A plugin that throws from its `metadata` getter or `settingsDescriptor()` is defended against in SettingsViewModel by catching `Throwable` (not just Exception) — explicitly to survive `AbstractMethodError`/`NoClassDefFoundError` linkage failures from misbehaving runtime plugins.

capabilities.name: DevicePlugin (hardware) contract
capabilities.behavior:
`interface DevicePlugin : Plugin` adds:
- `fun observeConnectionState(): StateFlow<ConnectionState>`
- `val pairingProfile: PairingProfile get() = PairingProfile()` (default CENTRAL_SCAN)
- `fun observePairingFault(): Flow<PairingFault?> = flowOf(null)`
- `fun connect(address: String, config: Map<String, String> = emptyMap())`
- `fun disconnect()` — must be a no-op when not connected
- `fun scan(): Flow<DiscoveredDevice>` — completes when scanning ends; cancel collection to stop early

`ConnectionState` (enum, 7 states): DISCONNECTED, SCANNING, CONNECTING, AUTHENTICATING, AUTH_FAILED, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING. No transition table is enforced by the platform — each driver owns its own machine and just exposes the StateFlow.

`PairingStyle`: CENTRAL_SCAN (phone is BLE central; scan → device list → user taps; e.g. Tandem) vs ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT (phone is BLE peripheral, advertises, the pump connects as central; e.g. Medtronic MiniMed 700-series). `PairingProfile(style, advertisedName: String?)` — advertisedName is the BLE name the user picks on the device's own pairing menu; null for central-scan.

`PairingFault` (5 values): PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED, ADVERTISE_FAILED, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, AUTH_FAILED, BOUND_ELSEWHERE. Exists because advertise-and-wait failures produce NO ConnectionState transition — the UI would otherwise have nothing to display.

`DiscoveredDevice(name, address, rssi: Int?, pluginId, metadata: Map<String,String> = emptyMap())`.

Connect timeout is a DOCUMENTED CONVENTION ONLY — 'typically 30 seconds' — not enforced by the interface or platform.

Config keys in use today: Tandem reads `config["pairingCode"]`; Medtronic reads `config["forceFirstPair"]` (`.toBoolean()`).
edge_cases: Medtronic's `connect(address, config)` IGNORES `address` entirely — in the inverted topology there is no pump address to dial.
Medtronic `scan()` emits a DiscoveredDevice only after a pump connects to the phone; there is no true scan.

capabilities.name: PluginMetadata and API versioning
capabilities.behavior:
`const val PLUGIN_API_VERSION = 5` in pump-driver-api/domain/plugin/PluginMetadata.kt. Documented version history in that file: v3 = BasalReading.controlIqMode renamed to activityMode (PumpActivityMode enum); v4 = BolusEvent.category field + BolusCategoryProvider capability; v5 = getFullHistoryLogs() overload added to PumpDriver and PumpStatus.

`data class PluginMetadata(id: String, name: String, version: String, apiVersion: Int, description: String = "", author: String = "", iconResName: String? = null, protocolName: String? = null)`.

Version enforcement is EXACT EQUALITY, checked in two places:
1. `PluginRegistry.initialize()` — `if (meta.apiVersion != PLUGIN_API_VERSION) { Timber.w("Plugin %s has API version %d, expected %d -- skipping"); continue }`. No crash.
2. `DexPluginLoader.loadJar()` — same check against the manifest's `apiVersion`, returns null (JAR rejected).

Protocol display convention: `protocolName` + `version` rendered as e.g. "Tandem v1.0.0" (SettingsViewModel: `m.protocolName?.let { "$it v${m.version}" }`). The plugin `version` field doubles as the protocol version — there is NO separate protocol-versioning infrastructure; bump `version` when BLE protocol handling changes.

Plugin ID pattern (shared constant `DexPluginLoader.VALID_PLUGIN_ID`, re-exported as `PluginRegistry.VALID_PLUGIN_ID`): `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,127}$` → 2 to 128 characters, must start with a letter.

When to bump PLUGIN_API_VERSION (documented): breaking changes to Plugin/DevicePlugin methods, capability interfaces, PluginContext constructor params, PluginEvent variants, SettingDescriptor/CardElement variants. Non-breaking additions do not require a bump.
edge_cases: DOC DRIFT: docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md states PLUGIN_API_VERSION is `2` (twice); the code says 5.

BROKEN SHIPPED EXAMPLE: plugins/example/src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.json declares `"apiVersion": 1`, and its README repeats 'currently 1'. With PLUGIN_API_VERSION=5 and exact-match enforcement, the reference example JAR would be rejected by DexPluginLoader today. (The Kotlin source `DemoGlucometerFactory` uses the constant, so only the JSON manifest is wrong.)
Version mismatch is silent to the user — only a Timber warning. The plugin simply does not appear in Available Plugins.

capabilities.name: PluginCapability enum and mutual exclusion
capabilities.behavior:
7 capabilities (pump-driver-api/domain/plugin/PluginCapability.kt): GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BGM_SOURCE, CALIBRATION_TARGET, DATA_SYNC, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER.

SINGLE_INSTANCE = {GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, CALIBRATION_TARGET, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER}
MULTI_INSTANCE = {BGM_SOURCE, DATA_SYNC}
A `companion object init {}` block asserts exhaustiveness at class-load: `check(SINGLE_INSTANCE + MULTI_INSTANCE == entries.toSet())` — adding a capability without classifying it throws at startup.

Mutual exclusion algorithm in `PluginRegistry.activatePlugin(pluginId)` (all under activationLock):
1. Look up plugin; unknown → `Result.failure(IllegalArgumentException("Unknown plugin: $id"))`.
2. Already in activePlugins → idempotent `Result.success(Unit)`, no callbacks.
3. Collect `conflictingIds`: for each of the plugin's SINGLE_INSTANCE capabilities, read `preferences.getActivePluginId(cap)`; add if non-null and != this id.
4. Call `plugin.onActivated()`; on throw → log + `Result.failure(e)` and the plugin is NOT registered active.
5. `activePlugins[id] = plugin`.
6. Persist: SINGLE_INSTANCE → `preferences.setActivePluginId(cap, id)`; MULTI_INSTANCE → `preferences.addActivePluginId(cap, id)`.
7. Deactivate each conflicting id via `deactivatePluginInternal`.
8. `updateStateFlows()`.

Deactivation (`deactivatePluginInternal`): remove from activePlugins (missing → `Result.failure(IllegalArgumentException("Plugin not active: $id"))`); call onDeactivated() in try/catch; clear preferences (SINGLE_INSTANCE only cleared if the stored id still equals this id — guards against clobbering the new owner; MULTI_INSTANCE → removeActivePluginId); updateStateFlows().

DATA_SYNC has NO capability interface — `getCapability()` returns null for it. It exists purely as an activation/mutual-exclusion tag (used by the Nightscout plugin and the example plugin).
edge_cases: Activating Medtronic while Tandem is active evicts Tandem from GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE and PUMP_STATUS simultaneously (pinned by PluginRegistryTest).
Conflict detection reads from PluginPreferences, not from the in-memory activePlugins map — if preferences and memory diverge, preferences win.
DOC DRIFT: docs list only 6 capabilities and omit BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER entirely.

capabilities.name: Capability interfaces (the read-only SDK surface)
capabilities.behavior:
All extend the empty marker `interface PluginCapabilityInterface`.

GlucoseSource: `fun observeReadings(): Flow<CgmReading>`, `suspend fun getCurrentReading(): Result<CgmReading>`.

InsulinSource: `suspend fun getIoB(): Result<IoBReading>`, `suspend fun getBasalRate(): Result<BasalReading>`, `suspend fun getBolusHistory(since: Instant, limits: SafetyLimits): Result<List<BolusEvent>>`.

PumpStatus: `getBatteryStatus()`, `getReservoirLevel()`, `getPumpSettings()`, `getPumpHardwareInfo()`, `getHistoryLogs(sinceSequence: Int)`, `getFullHistoryLogs(sinceSequence: Int)` (default = delegates to getHistoryLogs), `extractCgmFromHistoryLogs(records, limits)`, `extractBolusesFromHistoryLogs(records, limits)`, `extractBasalFromHistoryLogs(records, limits)`, `unpair()`, `autoReconnectIfPaired()`. (unpair/autoReconnectIfPaired are non-suspend with a TODO to make them suspend once the deprecated PumpConnectionManager is removed.)

BgmSource: `observeReadings(): Flow<BgmReading>`, `suspend getLatestReading(): Result<BgmReading>`.

CalibrationTarget: `suspend calibrate(bgValueMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant): Result<Unit>`, `suspend getCalibrationStatus(): Result<CalibrationStatus>`, plus companion `validateBgValue(bgValueMgDl: Int): Result<Unit>` which fails when outside `SafetyLimits.ABSOLUTE_MIN_GLUCOSE..ABSOLUTE_MAX_GLUCOSE` (20..500).

BolusCategoryProvider: `declaredCategories(): Set<String>`, `toPlatformCategory(pluginCategory: String): String?`. Tandem's implementation declares {CONTROL_IQ, BG_FOOD, BG_ONLY, FOOD_ONLY, OVERRIDE, QUICK, UNKNOWN} and maps CONTROL_IQ→AUTO_CORRECTION, BG_FOOD→FOOD_AND_CORRECTION, BG_ONLY→CORRECTION, FOOD_ONLY→FOOD, OVERRIDE→OVERRIDE, QUICK→OTHER, UNKNOWN→OTHER.

Domain models & their invariants: `CgmReading(glucoseMgDl: Int, trendArrow: CgmTrend, timestamp)` with `require(glucoseMgDl in 20..500)` (MIN_MG_DL=20, MAX_MG_DL=500). `BgmReading(glucoseMgDl, timestamp, meterName: String?)` with `require(glucoseMgDl in 20..500)`. `BolusEvent(units, isAutomated, isCorrection, correctionUnits=0f, mealUnits=0f, source="", category="", timestamp)` with require units/correctionUnits/mealUnits all >= 0f and <= `MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f`. `BasalReading(rate: Float, isAutomated, activityMode: PumpActivityMode, timestamp)`. `PumpActivityMode` = NONE/SLEEP/EXERCISE (deprecated typealias ControlIqMode). `CgmTrend` = DOUBLE_UP, SINGLE_UP, FORTY_FIVE_UP, FLAT, FORTY_FIVE_DOWN, SINGLE_DOWN, DOUBLE_DOWN, UNKNOWN. `IoBReading(iob: Float, timestamp)`. `BatteryStatus(percentage: Int, isCharging, timestamp)`. `ReservoirReading(unitsRemaining: Float, timestamp)`. `PumpSettings(firmwareVersion, serialNumber, modelNumber)`. `HistoryLogRecord(sequenceNumber: Int, rawBytesB64: String, eventTypeId: Int, pumpTimeSeconds: Long)`. `HistoryLogRange(firstSeq, lastSeq)` (unsigned-32 on the wire, stored signed Int; current pump values ~1.3M). `PumpHardwareInfo(serialNumber, modelNumber, partNumber, pumpRev, armSwVer, mspSwVer, configABits, configBBits, pcbaSn, pcbaRev, pumpFeatures: Map<String,Boolean>)`. `CalibrationStatus(lastCalibrationTime: Instant?, isCalibrationNeeded: Boolean, nextCalibrationDue: Instant?)`.

DELIBERATE OMISSION (load-bearing, stated in three places — docs, CONTRIBUTING.md, MedtronicDevicePlugin header): the SDK exposes NO insulin-delivery primitives. No bolus dosing, no basal-rate change, no pump-setting write, no therapeutic write surface at all. calibrate()/unpair()/autoReconnectIfPaired()/connect()/disconnect() are classified as session & lifecycle operations, not therapy. PRs adding therapeutic writes will not be merged. Enforcement is by API surface only — capability enforcement at the registry boundary (refusing to load plugins declaring capabilities outside the official enum) is documented as PLANNED, not implemented.
edge_cases: The extract* methods are contractually required to DROP out-of-range values, never clamp — enforced only by convention + unit tests, not by the interface.
getBolusHistory's SafetyLimits filtering is also convention-only ('not enforced by the interface itself but is a required safety contract').
Constructing a CgmReading/BgmReading/BolusEvent out of range throws IllegalArgumentException — so a driver that fails to filter crashes rather than emitting bad data.

capabilities.name: PluginRegistry — startup, state flows, runtime install/remove
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton class PluginRegistry @Inject constructor(factories: Set<PluginFactory>, preferences: PluginPreferences, eventBus: PluginEventBusImpl, @ApplicationContext context, credentialProvider: PumpCredentialProvider, debugLogger: DebugLogger, safetyLimitsStore: SafetyLimitsStore, featureGate: PluginFeatureGate)`.

Internal state: `plugins: ConcurrentHashMap<String, Plugin>`, `activePlugins: ConcurrentHashMap<String, Plugin>`, `activationLock = Any()`, `initialized: AtomicBoolean`, `_safetyLimits: MutableStateFlow(safetyLimitsStore.toSafetyLimits())`, `pluginSettingsStores: ConcurrentHashMap<String, PluginSettingsStoreImpl>`, `runtimePluginJars: ConcurrentHashMap<String, File>`, `compileTimePluginIds: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()`.

Exposed StateFlows: `availablePlugins: List<PluginMetadata>`, `activePumpPlugin: DevicePlugin?`, `activeGlucoseSource: DevicePlugin?`, `activeCalibrationTarget: DevicePlugin?`, `activeDataSyncPlugins: Set<Plugin>`, `activeBgmSources: Set<DevicePlugin>`, `allActivePlugins: List<Plugin>`, `runtimePlugins: List<RuntimePluginInfo>`.
`updateStateFlows()` resolution rules: activePumpPlugin = first active plugin declaring PUMP_STATUS **or** INSULIN_SOURCE, cast `as? DevicePlugin`; activeGlucoseSource = first with GLUCOSE_SOURCE `as? DevicePlugin`; activeCalibrationTarget = first with CALIBRATION_TARGET `as? DevicePlugin`; activeBgmSources = all with BGM_SOURCE, filterIsInstance<DevicePlugin>; activeDataSyncPlugins = all with DATA_SYNC (any Plugin).

`initialize()` (called from GlycemicGptApp.onCreate after Timber/Sentry/networkMonitor, before authManager.validateOnStartup): `check(initialized.compareAndSet(false, true)) { "PluginRegistry already initialized" }` — calling twice throws IllegalStateException. Then for each factory: (a) apiVersion != PLUGIN_API_VERSION → warn + skip; (b) `!featureGate.isEnabled(meta.id)` → info + skip; (c) validatePluginId(meta.id); (d) `compileTimePluginIds.add(meta.id)` BEFORE create — deliberately reserving the ID first so a runtime plugin cannot hijack a built-in ID if the built-in's init fails transiently; (e) createPluginContext + factory.create + plugin.initialize; on any Exception log + `pluginSettingsStores.remove(meta.id)` + skip. Then `discoverRuntimePlugins()`, then `_availablePlugins.value = plugins.values.map { it.metadata }`, then `restoreActivePlugins()`.

`restoreActivePlugins()`: for each SINGLE_INSTANCE cap, read the stored id; skip if the plugin isn't registered (absent plugin leaves the preference UNTOUCHED — deliberate, so a feature-gated-off plugin's selection survives re-enabling); if onActivated() throws → log + `preferences.clearActivePlugin(cap)`. Then for each MULTI_INSTANCE cap, iterate `getActivePluginIds(cap)`; on throw → `preferences.removeActivePluginId(cap, id)`.

`installRuntimePlugin(uri: Uri): Result<PluginMetadata>` (under lock): pluginFileManager.installPlugin(uri) → dexPluginLoader.loadJar(jarFile) (null → delete JAR, fail "Failed to load plugin from JAR") → validatePluginId → conflict with compileTimePluginIds → delete JAR + fail "Plugin ID 'X' conflicts with a built-in plugin" → conflict with already-loaded `plugins` → delete JAR + fail "Plugin ID 'X' is already installed" → createRestrictedPluginContext + factory.create + initialize → register in plugins/runtimePluginJars, `preferences.addInstalledRuntimePlugin(id)`, refresh availablePlugins + runtimePlugins flows. On any exception: log, remove settings store entry, delete the JAR, return failure. NOT auto-activated.

`removeRuntimePlugin(pluginId): Result<Unit>` (under lock): reject non-runtime ids; deactivate if active (failure logged, continues); `plugins.remove(id)` then `plugin.shutdown()` in try/catch; delete JAR via pluginFileManager; `preferences.removeInstalledRuntimePlugin(id)`; `pluginSettingsStores.remove(id)`; `context.deleteSharedPreferences("plugin_settings_$pluginId")`; refresh flows.

`refreshSafetyLimits()` (under lock): re-reads `safetyLimitsStore.toSafetyLimits()`, sets `_safetyLimits.value`, and publishes `PluginEvent.SafetyLimitsChanged(pluginId = PLATFORM_PLUGIN_ID, limits)` via `eventBus.publishPlatform`. `PLATFORM_PLUGIN_ID = "platform"`. Called from HomeViewModel (twice: initial refresh path and post-backend-sync path) right after `authRepository.refreshSafetyLimits()`.

Other API: `getPlugin(id): Plugin?`, `getPluginSettingsStore(id): PluginSettingsStore?`, `isRuntimePlugin(id): Boolean`.
`data class RuntimePluginInfo(metadata: PluginMetadata, jarFileName: String, isActive: Boolean)`.
edge_cases: `runtimePluginJars` is populated by discoverRuntimePlugins even for plugins whose IDs were also recorded in preferences — `preferences.addInstalledRuntimePlugin` is re-called on every discovery (idempotent set add).
`getInstalledRuntimePluginIds()` exists in PluginPreferences but is never read by the registry — the JAR files on disk are the source of truth; the preference set is write-only bookkeeping today.

A compile-time plugin that is not a DevicePlugin (e.g. Nightscout) never appears in activePumpPlugin/activeGlucoseSource because of the `as? DevicePlugin` cast — it only lands in activeDataSyncPlugins / allActivePlugins.
installRuntimePlugin holds `activationLock` across file I/O, DEX loading and reflection — a large JAR blocks activation/deactivation for the duration.

capabilities.name: PluginFeatureGate (per-plugin kill switch)
capabilities.behavior:
`fun interface PluginFeatureGate { fun isEnabled(pluginId: String): Boolean }`. Implementation `BuildConfigPluginFeatureGate`: `when (pluginId) { MedtronicDevicePlugin.PLUGIN_ID -> BuildConfig.MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED; else -> true }` — default ON; only an explicitly-disabled plugin is gated out. The gate references the driver's own canonical ID constant so the switch can never silently drift onto a nonexistent id (which would leave it always-enabled).

Build wiring: `app/build.gradle.kts` reads `System.getenv("MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED")?.lowercase() != "false"` and emits `buildConfigField("boolean", "MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED", …)` in two build variants (lines ~102 and ~150).

Semantics when gated off: the plugin is never created, so it is absent from Available Plugins (not selectable), has no pairing entry, and is never polled — fully invisible and inert. A persisted active-plugin preference is INTENTIONALLY left untouched, because this is an operator toggle: re-enabling restores the user's prior selection (restoreActivePlugins skips an absent plugin without disturbing the empty slot). Described as the mobile analogue of the backend's per-integration kill switches (e.g. `MEDTRONIC_CONNECT_ENABLED`).
edge_cases: The gate is only consulted for compile-time factories in `initialize()` — runtime-loaded plugins are NOT feature-gated.
If a gated-off plugin was the active GLUCOSE_SOURCE, that capability slot is simply empty until the gate is re-enabled; nothing warns the user.

capabilities.name: PluginPreferences (activation persistence)
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton class PluginPreferences` over `context.getSharedPreferences("plugin_prefs", MODE_PRIVATE)`.
Key schemes: single-instance → `"active_" + capability.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)` (String); multi-instance → `"active_multi_" + capability.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)` (StringSet); installed runtime plugins → `"installed_runtime_plugins"` (StringSet).
API: `getActivePluginId(cap): String?`, `setActivePluginId(cap, id)`, `clearActivePlugin(cap)`, `getActivePluginIds(cap): Set<String>`, `@Synchronized addActivePluginId/removeActivePluginId`, `getInstalledRuntimePluginIds()`, `@Synchronized addInstalledRuntimePlugin/removeInstalledRuntimePlugin`, `@Synchronized clear()`.
All writes use `.apply()` (async commit). The read-modify-write of the StringSets is guarded by `@Synchronized` on the PluginPreferences instance; the returned sets are defensively `.toSet()` copied (SharedPreferences StringSet must not be mutated in place).
edge_cases: `.apply()` means a process kill immediately after activation can lose the persisted selection.
`@Synchronized` only guards intra-process concurrency; PluginRegistry additionally holds activationLock around all of these calls.

capabilities.name: PluginSettingsStore (per-plugin key-value persistence)
capabilities.behavior:
Interface `PluginSettingsStore` (pump-driver-api): `getString(key, default="")`, `putString`, `getBoolean(key, default=false)`, `putBoolean`, `getInt(key, default=0)`, `putInt`, `getFloat(key, default=0f)`, `putFloat`, `remove(key)`. NO long accessor (this is why NightscoutSyncStore stores Longs as Strings).

Implementation `PluginSettingsStoreImpl(context, pluginId)` → `context.getSharedPreferences("plugin_settings_$pluginId", MODE_PRIVATE)`. All writes use `.apply()`. Note the file name uses the RAW plugin ID (unlike ScopedCredentialProvider, which sanitizes).

Documented behaviors: writes are immediate/synchronous from the caller's perspective; data survives deactivation and is restored on reactivation; data survives APK upgrades; data is namespaced per plugin ID; app uninstall clears it. Sensitive credentials must NOT go here — use `credentialProvider` (EncryptedSharedPreferences for compile-time plugins).

The registry keeps every created store in `pluginSettingsStores` so `getPluginSettingsStore(pluginId)` can hand it to the detail-screen/settings renderers.
edge_cases: A plugin ID containing filesystem-hostile characters would produce a malformed SharedPreferences filename — mitigated only because VALID_PLUGIN_ID already restricts to `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]`.
The SharedPreferences file for a removed runtime plugin is explicitly deleted by `context.deleteSharedPreferences("plugin_settings_$pluginId")`.

capabilities.name: PluginContext (what the platform hands a plugin)
capabilities.behavior:
`class PluginContext(androidContext: Context, pluginId: String, settingsStore: PluginSettingsStore, credentialProvider: PumpCredentialProvider, debugLogger: DebugLogger, eventBus: PluginEventBus, safetyLimits: StateFlow<SafetyLimits>, apiVersion: Int)`.

Compile-time construction (`PluginRegistry.createPluginContext`): full application Context, the app-wide `PumpCredentialProvider` (EncryptedSharedPreferences-backed), the shared `PluginEventBusImpl`, `_safetyLimits` StateFlow, `apiVersion = PLUGIN_API_VERSION`.
Runtime construction (`createRestrictedPluginContext`) → `RestrictedPluginContext.create(...)` with RestrictedContext + ScopedCredentialProvider.

`PumpCredentialProvider` interface: `getPairedAddress(): String?`, `getPairingCode(): String?`, `isPaired(): Boolean`, `savePairing(address, pairingCode)`, `clearPairing()`, `saveJpakeCredentials(derivedSecretHex, serverNonceHex)`, `getJpakeDerivedSecret(): String?`, `getJpakeServerNonce(): String?`, `clearJpakeCredentials()`.

`DebugLogger` interface: `enum Direction { TX, RX }`, `logPacket(direction, opcode: Int, opcodeName: String, txId: Int, cargoHex: String, cargoSize: Int, parsedValue: String? = null, error: String? = null)`, `updateLastPacket(opcode, direction, parsedValue, error)`. Security note in the interface doc: raw packet data (cargoHex, parsedValue) may contain glucose readings, insulin doses and device identifiers, so implementations must retain it only in debug builds and must never persist it unencrypted.
edge_cases: Compile-time plugins get the FULL application Context — documented as acceptable only for monorepo plugins.
`debugLogger` is shared unrestricted with runtime plugins (same instance as compile-time).

capabilities.name: DexPluginLoader (runtime JAR discovery and loading)
capabilities.behavior:
`class DexPluginLoader(context: Context)`. Directories: plugins dir = `File(context.filesDir, "plugins")` (`PLUGINS_DIR_NAME = "plugins"`); DEX output dir = `File(context.codeCacheDir, "plugin_dex")` (`DEX_OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "plugin_dex"`, created with mkdirs if absent).

`discover(): List<DiscoveredPlugin>` — returns emptyList if the plugins dir doesn't exist or isn't a directory; lists files with `extension == "jar"`; `mapNotNull { loadJar(it, dexOut) }`. One bad JAR never blocks the rest.

`loadJar(jarFile, dexOutputDir? = null): DiscoveredPlugin?` — wraps everything in try/catch(Exception) → log + null. Steps:
1. `DexClassLoader(jarFile.absolutePath, dexOut.absolutePath, /*librarySearchPath=*/null, context.classLoader)` — the APP'S classloader is the PARENT, which is what makes `pump-driver-api` classes resolvable from the plugin.
2. `readManifest(classLoader, jarFile)` — `classLoader.getResourceAsStream("META-INF/plugin.json")`; null → warn + skip. Reads at most `MAX_MANIFEST_SIZE = 65_536` chars into a CharArray; if `reader.read()` after that returns != -1 (i.e. more data exists), warn 'manifest exceeds 65536 bytes' and return null. Empty read (len<0) yields "". Then `PluginManifest.parse(json)`; IllegalArgumentException → log + null.
3. `if (manifest.apiVersion != PLUGIN_API_VERSION)` → warn + null.
4. `if (!VALID_PLUGIN_ID.matches(manifest.id))` → warn + null. (`VALID_PLUGIN_ID = Regex("^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,127}$")`, `internal`, reused by PluginRegistry.)
5. `classLoader.loadClass(manifest.factoryClass)`, `.getConstructor().newInstance() as? PluginFactory` — NO-ARG CONSTRUCTOR REQUIRED; a non-PluginFactory result → error log + null.
6. Returns `DiscoveredPlugin(factory, manifest, jarFile)`.

KNOWN LIMITATION (documented, deliberate): because the app's classloader is the parent, plugins can theoretically load and reflect over host app classes beyond the pump-driver-api interfaces. Full process-level isolation would require a separate Android process; rejected as too complex. The mitigation is the trust model — users explicitly install plugins after a security warning.
edge_cases: MAX_MANIFEST_SIZE is applied as 65,536 CHARS while the comment/log say bytes — for multi-byte UTF-8 the effective byte limit is larger.
`getResourceAsStream` walks the parent classloader chain first, so a `META-INF/plugin.json` present in the host APK could shadow the JAR's — not currently the case, but a porting hazard.
JAR files must be read-only on disk (PluginFileManager calls setReadOnly()) because Android's DexClassLoader rejects writable DEX files.
No signature verification, no checksum, no allowlist of packages — any DEX in the JAR runs in-process.

capabilities.name: PluginManifest (META-INF/plugin.json format and parsing)
capabilities.behavior:
`data class PluginManifest(factoryClass: String, apiVersion: Int, id: String, name: String, version: String, author: String = "", description: String = "")`. `const val MANIFEST_PATH = "META-INF/plugin.json"`.

`parse(json: String): PluginManifest` using org.json.JSONObject:
- Invalid JSON → `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid plugin manifest JSON", cause)`.
- `factoryClass` blank/missing → "Manifest missing required field: factoryClass".
- `id` blank/missing → "Manifest missing required field: id".
- `name` blank/missing → "Manifest missing required field: name".
- `version` blank/missing → "Manifest missing required field: version".
- `apiVersion` missing or non-int → "Manifest missing or invalid required field: apiVersion".
- `apiVersion < 1` → "Manifest apiVersion must be >= 1, got: N".
- `author`, `description` optional, default "".
Field order of validation matters for error reporting: factoryClass, id, name, version, then apiVersion.

Example manifest (plugins/example/src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.json):
{"factoryClass":"com.example.glycemicgpt.plugin.DemoGlucometerFactory","apiVersion":1,"id":"com.example.glycemicgpt.demo-glucometer","name":"Demo Glucometer","version":"1.0.0","author":"GlycemicGPT","description":"…"}
edge_cases: The manifest declares id/name/version/author/description INDEPENDENTLY of the factory's PluginMetadata. The registry validates and de-conflicts using the MANIFEST id, but the plugin registered in `plugins[...]` is keyed by manifest id while `availablePlugins`/`runtimePlugins` show `plugin.metadata` — a plugin whose metadata.id differs from its manifest id would display inconsistently.
apiVersion>=1 check is redundant with the exact-match check in DexPluginLoader but produces a distinct error message.

capabilities.name: PluginFileManager (JAR install/remove on disk)
capabilities.behavior:
`class PluginFileManager(context)`. pluginsDir = `File(context.filesDir, "plugins")`.
Constants: `MAX_PLUGIN_SIZE_BYTES = 50L * 1024 * 1024` (52,428,800 bytes = 50 MB); `ZIP_MAGIC = byteArrayOf(0x50, 0x4B, 0x03, 0x04)` ("PK\x03\x04").

`installPlugin(sourceUri: Uri): Result<File>` steps, in order:
1. mkdirs the plugins dir if missing.
2. Derive raw filename: `sourceUri.lastPathSegment?.substringAfterLast('/')?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: "plugin_${System.currentTimeMillis()}.jar"`.
3. Must end with `.jar` (case-insensitive) else `Result.failure(IllegalArgumentException("Only .jar files are accepted, got: $rawName"))`.
4. Sanitize: `fileName.replace(Regex("[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]"), "_")`.
5. Canonical-path check: `if (!destCanonical.path.startsWith(dirCanonical.path + File.separator))` → `SecurityException("Plugin filename resolves outside plugins directory")`.
6. `if (destFile.exists())` → `IllegalArgumentException("Plugin file already exists: <name>")` (no overwrite/upgrade path).
7. `context.contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)`; null → `IOException("Cannot open URI: $uri")`.
8. Stream copy with `ByteArray(DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE)` (Kotlin default = 8192), accumulating totalBytes; exceeding MAX_PLUGIN_SIZE_BYTES → delete partial file + failure "Plugin file exceeds maximum size of 50 MB".
9. `isValidZip(destFile)`: file length >= 4 and first 4 bytes == ZIP_MAGIC; else delete + "File is not a valid JAR/ZIP archive".
10. `destFile.setReadOnly()` — required because DexClassLoader rejects writable DEX files.
Catches IOException and SecurityException at the top level → logged failure.

`removePlugin(jarFile): Boolean` — false if not exists; canonical-path containment check with `+ File.separator` appended to prevent prefix collisions (e.g. "plugins_evil/"); `jarFile.setWritable(true)` then `delete()`.

`listInstalledJars(): List<File>` — files with `extension == "jar"`, empty when the dir is missing.
edge_cases: Size is checked DURING the copy, not from a Content-Length — a stream that exceeds the cap writes up to 50 MB before being deleted.
ZIP magic is checked AFTER the full copy, not before.
No versioning/upgrade: reinstalling the same filename fails; the user must Remove first.
`listInstalledJars()` is defined but never called by the registry.

capabilities.name: RestrictedPluginContext / RestrictedContext sandbox
capabilities.behavior:
`object RestrictedPluginContext.create(baseContext, pluginId, settingsStore, debugLogger, eventBus, safetyLimits): PluginContext` — `require(pluginId.isNotBlank())`, wraps baseContext in `RestrictedContext`, uses `ScopedCredentialProvider(pluginId, baseContext)` (the UNRESTRICTED base context, because SharedPreferences is per-app sandboxed anyway and the ID namespace prevents cross-plugin reads), passes settingsStore/debugLogger/eventBus/safetyLimits through unchanged, `apiVersion = PLUGIN_API_VERSION`.

`internal class RestrictedContext(base) : ContextWrapper(base)` — every blocked method calls `denied(op)` = `throw SecurityException("Runtime plugins cannot call $op")`.
BLOCKED (complete list as coded): getBaseContext; startActivity(Intent), startActivity(Intent, Bundle); startActivities(Array), startActivities(Array, Bundle); startService, startForegroundService, stopService, bindService; getContentResolver; sendBroadcast(Intent), sendBroadcast(Intent, String); sendOrderedBroadcast (3 overloads); registerReceiver (4 overloads); getSharedPreferences; openFileOutput, openFileInput, deleteFile, getDir; getDatabasePath, openOrCreateDatabase (2 overloads), deleteDatabase; createDeviceProtectedStorageContext; createPackageContext.
TRAPPED: `getApplicationContext(): Context = this` — returns the restricted wrapper itself so a plugin cannot escape by walking up.
ALLOWLISTED `getSystemService(name)`: throws unless name ∈ ALLOWED_SYSTEM_SERVICES = {Context.BLUETOOTH_SERVICE, LOCATION_SERVICE, POWER_SERVICE, ALARM_SERVICE, SENSOR_SERVICE, USB_SERVICE, WIFI_SERVICE}. WINDOW_SERVICE is INTENTIONALLY EXCLUDED with an in-code comment: plugins don't need display metrics, and WindowManager can add overlay views if SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is held.
STILL ALLOWED (inherited, not overridden): getFilesDir, getCacheDir, getPackageName, getResources, getAssets, etc.

DESIGN PHILOSOPHY (explicit, load-bearing): 'Safety enforcement comes from SafetyLimits (synced from the backend), not from blanket Context restrictions.' Plugins need hardware services to function as BLE pump/CGM drivers; only non-hardware services are blocked, to prevent data exfiltration.

Compile-time plugins receive the FULL unrestricted PluginContext — no sandbox at all.
edge_cases: `getSystemService(Class<T>)` (the typed overload) is NOT overridden — only the String-name overload is intercepted. On Android the typed overload delegates to the String form via getSystemServiceName, so it is covered in practice, but this is implicit, not explicit.
The sandbox is a language-level wrapper only: a plugin holding a reference obtained through reflection over host classes bypasses it entirely (acknowledged known limitation).

filesDir/cacheDir remain fully accessible, so a runtime plugin can read/write anywhere in the app's file sandbox — including other plugins' JARs and the SharedPreferences XML files on disk (getSharedPreferences is blocked, but raw file access to shared_prefs is not).

capabilities.name: ScopedCredentialProvider (per-runtime-plugin credential isolation)
capabilities.behavior:
`internal class ScopedCredentialProvider(pluginId, context) : PumpCredentialProvider` over `context.getSharedPreferences("plugin_creds_${sanitizeId(pluginId)}", MODE_PRIVATE)`.
Keys: `paired_address`, `pairing_code`, `jpake_derived_secret`, `jpake_server_nonce`.
Behavior: `isPaired()` = `prefs.contains("paired_address")`; `savePairing` writes address+code together; `clearPairing` removes both; JPAKE pair saved/cleared together; all writes `.apply()`.
`sanitizeId(pluginId) = pluginId.replace(Regex("[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]"), "_")` — deliberately PRESERVES dots, hyphens and underscores so `com.foo.bar-baz` and `com.foo.bar.baz` stay distinct namespaces; only path-unsafe characters (slashes, null bytes) are stripped.

EXPLICIT ACCEPTED RISK documented in-code: runtime plugins use REGULAR SharedPreferences, not EncryptedSharedPreferences, because runtime plugins cannot access the AndroidX Security library. On rooted/debug devices these credentials are readable via `run-as`. Accepted for the current trust model (user-installed plugins for personal device pairing); migration to EncryptedSharedPreferences is called out as required if the threat model changes to include adversarial plugins.
Compile-time plugins get the app's EncryptedSharedPreferences-backed provider instead.
edge_cases: Removing a runtime plugin deletes `plugin_settings_<id>` but does NOT delete `plugin_creds_<sanitized id>` — pairing credentials survive plugin removal and reinstall.

capabilities.name: PluginEventBus (cross-plugin event bus)
capabilities.behavior:
Interface `PluginEventBus { fun publish(event: PluginEvent); fun <T : PluginEvent> subscribe(eventType: KClass<T>): Flow<T> }` plus `inline fun <reified T : PluginEvent> PluginEventBus.subscribe(): Flow<T> = subscribe(T::class)`.

`@Singleton class PluginEventBusImpl : PluginEventBus`:
- backing = `MutableSharedFlow<PluginEvent>(extraBufferCapacity = 256, onBufferOverflow = BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST)`. replay = 0 (default) — a late subscriber sees NO history.
- `publish(event)`: if `event::class in PluginEvent.PLATFORM_ONLY` → `Timber.w("Plugin %s attempted to publish platform-only event %s -- blocked")` and RETURN (silently dropped, no exception). Otherwise `tryEmit`; on false → `Timber.w("Event bus buffer full, dropping event: …")`.
- `internal fun publishPlatform(event)`: bypasses the platform-only check; `internal` visibility restricts it to the `:app` module, so plugins in separate Gradle modules cannot call it.
- `subscribe(eventType)` = `events.filterIsInstance(eventType)` on the asSharedFlow() view.

Event types (sealed class PluginEvent, all carry `pluginId: String`):
- `NewGlucoseReading(pluginId, reading: CgmReading)`
- `NewBgmReading(pluginId, reading: BgmReading)`
- `InsulinDelivered(pluginId, event: BolusEvent)`
- `DeviceConnected(pluginId)`
- `DeviceDisconnected(pluginId)`
- `CalibrationRequested(pluginId, bgValueMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant)` — `init { require(bgValueMgDl in 20..500) }` — SAFETY VALIDATION AT CONSTRUCTION.
- `CalibrationCompleted(pluginId, success: Boolean, message: String)`
- `SafetyLimitsChanged(pluginId, limits: SafetyLimits)` — PLATFORM ONLY.
`companion object { val PLATFORM_ONLY: Set<KClass<out PluginEvent>> = setOf(SafetyLimitsChanged::class) }`.

Documented calibration flow: BGM plugin gets fingerstick → publishes NewBgmReading → publishes CalibrationRequested → CGM plugin (subscribed) calibrates the device → publishes CalibrationCompleted → BGM plugin updates its UI.

Plugins should observe safety limits via `PluginContext.safetyLimits` (a StateFlow, always has a current value) rather than subscribing to SafetyLimitsChanged.
edge_cases: Buffer overflow DROPS THE OLDEST event silently (only a warning log) — the bus provides NO delivery guarantee. Nothing safety-critical currently depends on it, but a calibration request could be dropped under load.
replay=0 means a plugin that subscribes after an event was published misses it entirely — there is no 'latest value' semantics.
The platform-only check is by exact KClass identity; a plugin subclassing a platform-only event is impossible (sealed class), so the check is sound.
No `:app`-module plugin (like NightscoutSourcePlugin) is prevented from calling publishPlatform — the `internal` guard is module-scoped, not plugin-scoped.

capabilities.name: Declarative settings UI descriptors
capabilities.behavior:
`sealed class SettingDescriptor { abstract val key: String }` with 6 variants, each running `requireValidKey(key)` in its init against `VALID_KEY = Regex("^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}$")` (1–128 chars, must start with a letter):
- `TextInput(key, label, hint = "", sensitive = false)` — sensitive masks with PasswordVisualTransformation.
- `Toggle(key, label, description = "")`
- `Slider(key, label, min: Float, max: Float, step: Float = 1f, unit: String = "")` — init also requires `min < max`, `step > 0`, `step <= max - min`.
- `Dropdown(key, label, options: List<DropdownOption>)` — init requires options non-empty.
- `ActionButton(key, label, style: ButtonStyle = DEFAULT)`
- `InfoText(key, text)`
`data class DropdownOption(value: String, label: String)` — requires value non-blank.
`enum ButtonStyle { DEFAULT, PRIMARY, DESTRUCTIVE }`.
`data class PluginSettingsSection(title: String, items: List<SettingDescriptor>)`.
`data class PluginSettingsDescriptor(sections: List<PluginSettingsSection>)` — init requires all setting keys across ALL sections to be globally unique, error message lists the duplicates.
edge_cases: Constructing an invalid descriptor throws IllegalArgumentException — inside a plugin's settingsDescriptor(), which the platform calls from the UI thread. SettingsViewModel catches Throwable around this call for exactly this reason.

capabilities.name: Declarative dashboard card + detail screen descriptors
capabilities.behavior:
`data class DashboardCardDescriptor(id: String, title: String, priority: Int = 100, elements: List<CardElement>, hasDetail: Boolean = false)` — init requires id and title non-blank. LOWER priority = higher on the dashboard. Documented convention: platform core cards (GlucoseHero, TrendChart, TimeInRange) occupy priority 0–50; plugin cards should use 100+.

`sealed class CardElement` (9 variants):
- `LargeValue(value: String, unit: String = "", color: UiColor = DEFAULT)`
- `Label(text: String, style: LabelStyle = BODY)`
- `StatusBadge(text: String, color: UiColor)`
- `ProgressBar(value: Float, max: Float, label: String = "")` — init requires max and value finite, max > 0f, value in 0f..max.
- `IconValue(icon: PluginIcon, value: String, label: String = "")`
- `SparkLine(values: List<Float>, label: String = "")` — init requires non-empty and all finite.
- `Row(elements)` / `Column(elements)` — init requires non-empty.
- `Spacer(heightDp: Int = 8)` — init requires heightDp >= 0.
`enum UiColor { DEFAULT, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, INFO, MUTED }`.
`enum LabelStyle { TITLE, SUBTITLE, BODY, CAPTION }`.
`enum PluginIcon` (13): BLUETOOTH, BATTERY, RESERVOIR, INSULIN, GLUCOSE, HEART_RATE, SYNC, WARNING, CHECK, CLOCK, SETTINGS, SIGNAL, THERMOMETER.

`data class DetailScreenDescriptor(title: String, elements: List<DetailElement>)` — init requires title non-blank, `elements.size <= MAX_ELEMENTS` where `MAX_ELEMENTS = 100` (explicitly 'to prevent UI DoS'), and no duplicate keys among Interactive elements.
`sealed class DetailElement { Display(element: CardElement); Interactive(setting: SettingDescriptor); SectionHeader(title: String) }` — SectionHeader requires non-blank title. Deliberately reuses CardElement and SettingDescriptor rather than duplicating types.
edge_cases: Row/Column nesting is unbounded at the descriptor level; the RENDERER caps depth (see renderer capability).
DashboardCardDescriptor does not validate element count — only the detail screen does.

capabilities.name: Dashboard card renderer (platform-side)
capabilities.behavior:
`PluginDashboardCardRenderer(card, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null)` — Material 3 `Card`, testTag `plugin_card_${card.id}`, 16.dp padding. Header Row: card.title (titleSmall, weight 1f) + when onClick != null a `KeyboardArrowRight` icon (20.dp, onSurfaceVariant, contentDescription 'View details'). 8.dp Spacer, then each element via `RenderElement(element, depth = 0)`. When onClick != null the card gets `Modifier.clickable(role = Role.Button, onClick)`.

`internal const val MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 5`; `RenderElement` returns immediately when `depth > MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`. Row/Column recurse with `depth + 1`.

Element rendering specifics:
- LargeValue → Row(Alignment.Bottom): value in headlineLarge tinted by UiColor; unit (if non-empty) after a 4.dp spacer in bodyMedium/onSurfaceVariant.
- Label → TITLE=titleMedium, SUBTITLE=titleSmall, BODY=bodyMedium, CAPTION=bodySmall.
- StatusBadge → Surface with RoundedCornerShape(4.dp), background = color.copy(alpha = 0.12f), text labelSmall in the resolved color, padding h=8.dp v=4.dp.
- ProgressBar → optional label (bodySmall/onSurfaceVariant) + 4.dp spacer, then LinearProgressIndicator with `progress = (value / max).coerceIn(0f, 1f)`.
- IconValue → 16.dp icon (onSurfaceVariant), 6.dp spacer, value bodyMedium, optional label after 4.dp spacer in bodySmall/onSurfaceVariant.
- SparkLine → optional label + 4.dp spacer; Canvas fillMaxWidth height 40.dp, stroke width 2.dp converted via LocalDensity; returns early if values.size < 2; y normalized over `range = (max - min).coerceAtLeast(1f)`; `stepX = width / (size - 1)`; drawn as consecutive line segments in colorScheme.primary.
- Row → fillMaxWidth, Arrangement.SpaceBetween, CenterVertically.
- Column → fillMaxWidth.
- Spacer → Modifier.height(element.heightDp.dp).

UiColor mapping: DEFAULT→colorScheme.onSurface, SUCCESS→Color(0xFF4CAF50), WARNING→Color(0xFFFF9800), ERROR→colorScheme.error, INFO→colorScheme.primary, MUTED→colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant.
PluginIcon mapping: BLUETOOTH→Icons.Default.Bluetooth, BATTERY→Battery5Bar, RESERVOIR→LocalDrink, INSULIN→Medication, GLUCOSE→MonitorHeart, HEART_RATE→Favorite, SYNC→Sync, WARNING→Warning, CHECK→Check, CLOCK→Schedule, SETTINGS→Settings, SIGNAL→SignalCellularAlt, THERMOMETER→DeviceThermostat.

Home integration: HomeViewModel exposes `pluginCards: StateFlow<List<PluginCard>>` = `pluginRegistry.allActivePlugins.flatMapLatest { … combine(each plugin.observeDashboardCards()) … sortedBy { it.card.priority } }` with `stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList())`; empty plugin list short-circuits to `flowOf(emptyList())`. HomeScreen re-sorts by priority (memoized), inserts a 12.dp Spacer before each card, and passes onClick only when `card.hasDetail`.
HomeViewModel also exposes `activePluginIds: StateFlow<List<String>>` = active plugin metadata ids SORTED — sorted explicitly because allActivePlugins is backed by a ConcurrentHashMap with undefined iteration order, which would otherwise shuffle the dashboard brand badges between emissions.
edge_cases: `observeDashboardCards()` is collected directly on the ViewModel scope with no error boundary — a plugin flow that throws propagates into the combine.
Elements nested deeper than 5 are silently omitted, not truncated with an indicator.

capabilities.name: Settings renderer and plugin detail screen
capabilities.behavior:
`PluginSettingsRenderer(descriptor, settingsStore: PluginSettingsStore? = null, onAction: (key) -> Unit = {})` — renders each section with a 16.dp gap between sections, section title in titleSmall/colorScheme.primary with 8.dp bottom padding, and 8.dp between items.
`SettingItem` dispatch: TextInput/Toggle/Slider/Dropdown are rendered ONLY when a store is non-null (they cannot be read or persisted without one); ActionButton and InfoText always render. This is how the pump settings card renders a plugin's InfoText notes with no store.
Persistence semantics per control:
- TextInput: local state seeded from `store.getString(key)`; persisted `onFocusChanged { if (!it.isFocused) store.putString(key, value) }` — i.e. ON FOCUS LOSS, not on each keystroke.
- Toggle: `store.getBoolean(key)`, writes immediately in onCheckedChange.
- Slider: seeded from `store.getFloat(key, descriptor.min).coerceIn(min, max)`; persisted in `onValueChangeFinished` with a coerceIn; step count = `((max - min) / step).toInt() - 1` then `coerceAtLeast(0)`; display formats as integer when `step >= 1f` else "%.1f", suffixed with unit.
- Dropdown: value read live from `store.getString(key)`; label falls back to the first option's label when the stored value matches nothing; selection writes `store.putString(key, option.value)`.
- ActionButton: PRIMARY→filled Button, DESTRUCTIVE→OutlinedButton with contentColor = colorScheme.error, DEFAULT→OutlinedButton; all fillMaxWidth; onClick → `onAction(key)`.
- InfoText: bodySmall/onSurfaceVariant.

`PluginDetailScreen(pluginId, cardId, onBack, viewModel = hiltViewModel())` — Scaffold + TopAppBar titled from the descriptor (empty while loading) with a back arrow; body is a verticalScroll Column with 16.dp padding. Renders error text (colorScheme.error) if error != null, else 'Loading...' while descriptor is null, else iterates elements: Display→RenderElement + 8.dp spacer; Interactive→SettingItem (only when store != null) + 8.dp spacer; SectionHeader→16.dp spacer + titleSmall/primary title with 8.dp bottom padding.

`PluginDetailViewModel.load(pluginId, cardId)`: early-returns if already loaded with the same cardId; resets error/descriptor and cancels the previous collection job; `pluginRegistry.getPlugin(pluginId)` null → error 'Plugin not found'; sets `_settingsStore` from `pluginRegistry.getPluginSettingsStore(pluginId)`; `plugin.observeDetailScreen(cardId)` null → error 'No detail available for this card'; otherwise collects `flow.flowOn(Dispatchers.IO).conflate()` in viewModelScope, clearing the error on each emission; CancellationException rethrown, other Exception → log + error 'Plugin encountered an error loading detail content'.
`onAction(key)`: launches on Dispatchers.IO, calls `plugin.onDetailAction(cardId, key)` in try/catch → on failure sets error 'Action could not be completed'.

Navigation: `Screen.PluginDetail` route = `"plugin_detail/{pluginId}/{cardId}"`; navigation uses `Uri.encode(pluginId)` / `Uri.encode(cardId)`; both args are `NavType.StringType`.
edge_cases: TextInput persists only on focus loss — navigating away without blurring the field loses the edit.
Interactive detail elements are silently skipped when the plugin has no settings store registered.
The 'load' guard checks `plugin != null && this.cardId == cardId` — changing pluginId while keeping the same cardId would NOT reload.

capabilities.name: Settings > Plugins UI (activation, custom plugin install/remove)
capabilities.behavior:
SettingsScreen renders a 'Plugins' section containing: the generic pump pairing card (shown whenever `state.activePumpPluginId != null`, i.e. any pump DevicePlugin is active), an 'Available Plugins' card, and a 'Custom Plugins' card.

Available Plugins list: driven by `SettingsUiState.visibleAvailablePlugins`, a DERIVED property (deliberately computed in the state class, not filtered at copy() sites, 'so it can never go stale'): `availablePlugins.filter { backendConfigured || it.id != NightscoutSourcePlugin.PLUGIN_ID || it.id in activePluginIds }`. Rationale (GLY-146): the Nightscout source is cloud-mediated, so in BLE-only mode its activation control is withheld — arming it could only schedule work the request layer refuses. An already-active instance stays listed so Deactivate stays reachable.
Each row shows `plugin.name` and `v${plugin.version}`, plus Activate (testTag `activate_plugin_<id>`) or Deactivate (testTag `deactivate_plugin_<id>`, error-colored OutlinedButton).

Custom Plugins card: title 'Custom Plugins'; a persistent red warning row with a Warning icon: 'Custom plugins are not verified by GlycemicGPT. Only install plugins from sources you trust.' (testTag `plugin_trust_warning`); an error banner (errorContainer card + Dismiss TextButton) when `pluginInstallError != null`; one row per RuntimePluginInfo showing name and `v<version>[ by <author>]` with Activate/Deactivate plus a Remove button (testTag `remove_plugin_<id>`); an 'Add Plugin' OutlinedButton (testTag `add_plugin_button`) launching `ActivityResultContracts.GetContent()` with MIME `application/java-archive`.

Confirmation dialogs (both required, no direct action):
- Deactivate: title 'Deactivate Plugin', body 'Deactivating this plugin may stop glucose monitoring, insulin tracking, or other services it provides. Are you sure?'. `deactivatePlugin(id)` is @Deprecated and simply forwards to `showDeactivateConfirm(id)`.
- Remove: title 'Remove Plugin', body 'This will permanently remove the plugin and delete its settings. This cannot be undone.'

ViewModel wiring: `activatePlugin(id)` calls the registry synchronously and refreshes `activePluginIds` (+ withActivePumpFields()); `installPlugin(uri)` and `confirmRemovePlugin()` run in viewModelScope and refresh availablePlugins/activePluginIds/runtimePlugins; install failure sets `pluginInstallError = e.message ?: "Failed to install plugin"`; `clearPluginInstallError()` dismisses it.
`withActivePumpFields()` reads `plugin.metadata` and `plugin.settingsDescriptor()` in SEPARATE try/catch(Throwable) blocks on purpose: a descriptor failure drops only the informational notes and keeps the pump card, whereas losing metadata necessarily drops the card (id/name are required).
`infoNotesOnly()` reduces a plugin's settings descriptor to only its `SettingDescriptor.InfoText` items (dropping empty sections, returning null if nothing remains) — because the generic pump card owns live pairing status and the pair/unpair actions, so interactive plugin settings never belong on it.
edge_cases: There is no per-plugin settings sub-screen wired for arbitrary plugins today — only InfoText notes surfaced on the pump card, plus card→detail-screen navigation from the dashboard.
Removing a runtime plugin while it is active deactivates it first; a deactivation failure is logged and removal proceeds anyway.

capabilities.name: Legacy adapters (plugin registry → deprecated pump interfaces)
capabilities.behavior:
Four @Singleton adapters bridge the four @Deprecated pump interfaces onto the registry, so pre-plugin consumers (HomeViewModel, PumpPollingOrchestrator, PumpConnectionService, pairing screens) compile unchanged. Bound in `PluginModule` via @Binds @Singleton.

`PumpDriverAdapter : PumpDriver` — every method resolves through the registry's StateFlows: connect/disconnect/getIoB/getBasalRate/getBolusHistory/getPumpSettings/getBatteryStatus/getReservoirLevel/getHistoryLogs/getFullHistoryLogs/getPumpHardwareInfo go through `registry.activePumpPlugin.value` (`asInsulinSource()` / `asPumpStatus()`); `getCgmStatus()` goes through `registry.activeGlucoseSource.value?.asGlucoseSource()?.getCurrentReading()`. Missing plugin/capability → `Result.failure(NoActivePluginException())` (default message 'No active plugin for this capability'). connect/disconnect wrap in try/catch that RETHROWS CancellationException and converts other Exceptions to Result.failure. `observeConnectionState()` = `registry.activePumpPlugin.flatMapLatest { it?.observeConnectionState() ?: flowOf(ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED) }`.

`PumpConnectionAdapter : PumpConnectionManager` — owns `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate)`. `connectionState` = flatMapLatest over activePumpPlugin, `stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, DISCONNECTED)`. `pairingProfile` = map to `plugin?.pairingProfile ?: PairingProfile()`, Eagerly. `pairingFault` = flatMapLatest to `plugin?.observePairingFault() ?: flowOf(null)`, Eagerly. `connect(address, pairingCode)` logs a warning and returns when no active pump plugin, else calls `plugin.connect(address, mapOf("pairingCode" to code))` (empty map when code is null). `disconnect()`, `unpair()` (via asPumpStatus()), `autoReconnectIfPaired()` (via asPumpStatus()) are null-safe no-ops.

`PumpScannerAdapter : PumpScanner` — `scan()` returns `emptyFlow()` when no active pump plugin; otherwise maps DiscoveredDevice → `DiscoveredPump(name, address, rssi = device.rssi ?: 0)`.

`HistoryLogParserAdapter : HistoryLogParser` — the three extract* methods delegate to `activePumpPlugin.value?.asPumpStatus()`, returning `emptyList()` when absent.
edge_cases: SAFETY: HistoryLogParserAdapter returns emptyList() (not an error) when no plugin is active — a caller cannot distinguish 'no records' from 'no driver'.
PumpDriverAdapter.getCgmStatus reads the GLUCOSE_SOURCE slot while every other read reads the PUMP slot — with a CGM-only plugin active alongside a pump these can be different plugins.
PumpConnectionAdapter's `SharingStarted.Eagerly` StateFlows are created on Dispatchers.Main.immediate at injection time.

capabilities.name: SafetyLimits: definition, clamping, and distribution to plugins
capabilities.behavior:
`data class SafetyLimits(minGlucoseMgDl = 20, maxGlucoseMgDl = 500, maxBasalRateMilliunits = 15_000, maxBolusDoseMilliunits = 25_000)`.
Constants: DEFAULT_MIN_GLUCOSE=20, DEFAULT_MAX_GLUCOSE=500, DEFAULT_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS=15_000 (15 U/hr, Tandem hardware max), DEFAULT_MAX_BOLUS_MILLIUNITS=25_000 (25 U single dose). ABSOLUTE_* aliases equal the DEFAULT_* values — 'no backend configuration may widen these'; rationale in-code: CGM sensors are unreliable below ~20 and above ~500 mg/dL.
Constructor `init` REQUIREs: min >= 20; max <= 500; min < max; maxBasalRateMilliunits in 1..15_000; maxBolusDoseMilliunits in 1..25_000 — throws for programmatic callers.
`safeOf(...)`: the lenient factory for untrusted/external data — `clampedMin = min.coerceIn(20, 499)`, `clampedMax = max.coerceIn(clampedMin + 1, 500)`, `clampedBasal = basal.coerceIn(1, 15_000)`, `clampedBolus = bolus.coerceIn(1, 25_000)`. Clamps instead of throwing 'where a crash would be worse than clamped values'.
Documented caveat: the absolute bounds are currently based on TANDEM hardware limits (shared across t:slim X2 and Mobi); other pump hardware may require revisiting these constants.

`SafetyLimitsStore` (`safety_limits` SharedPreferences, keys min_glucose/max_glucose/max_basal/max_bolus/last_fetched_ms): only `updateAll(min, max, basal, bolus)` from backend sync may write — 'The mobile app NEVER allows local override of safety limits.' updateAll runs `SafetyLimits.safeOf(...)` BEFORE persisting so even direct property reads return safe values, and uses `.commit()` (synchronous) for the whole 5-field transaction. `toSafetyLimits()` also re-applies safeOf. `isStale(maxAgeMs = STALE_THRESHOLD_MS)` with `STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000L` (1 hour). `clear()` on logout resets to defaults.

Distribution: PluginRegistry seeds `_safetyLimits` at construction from `safetyLimitsStore.toSafetyLimits()`, exposes it to every plugin as `PluginContext.safetyLimits: StateFlow<SafetyLimits>`, and `refreshSafetyLimits()` re-reads + republishes. HomeViewModel calls `authRepository.refreshSafetyLimits()` then `pluginRegistry.refreshSafetyLimits()` in two places (initial load path ~line 223 and post-backend-sync path ~line 422).

Plugin responsibilities (documented, convention-enforced): read safetyLimits from PluginContext; DROP out-of-range values, never clamp; pass limits into all extract* methods; never publish SafetyLimitsChanged. CONTRIBUTING.md adds: 'when a reading falls outside the limits, plugins must discard it (do not return, emit, or persist it) and log the rejection with the violated limit.'
edge_cases: Two independent validation paths exist: SafetyLimits (user-configurable, narrowable) AND the domain models' own hard requires (20..500 mg/dL, <=25 U). A driver can pass SafetyLimits and still throw at CgmReading construction if limits were widened — impossible today since ABSOLUTE == DEFAULT.

There is no unit conversion anywhere in this subsystem for glucose: everything is mg/dL end to end. Insulin has TWO units in play — SafetyLimits uses MILLIUNITS (15_000 / 25_000) while BolusEvent/BasalReading use FLOAT UNITS (25f / 15f). The only conversion is NightscoutDataMapper's `MAX_BASAL_RATE_U_HR = ABSOLUTE_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS / 1000f`.
If the store is stale (>1 hour), plugins still receive the last cached limits — staleness is exposed via isStale() but the registry does not consult it.

capabilities.name: Nightscout source plugin (cloud-mediated DATA_SYNC plugin)
capabilities.behavior:
`NightscoutSourcePlugin(syncManager, store, connectionsProvider: suspend () -> List<NightscoutConnectionDto>) : Plugin` — Story 43.8. NOT a device plugin: it talks to no hardware. It pulls the user's Nightscout-sourced data from the GlycemicGPT BACKEND's read API (the only Nightscout client lives in the Python backend) into the same Room tables the BLE plugins write, so the dashboard populates without a second Nightscout client on Android.

METADATA: id `com.glycemicgpt.nightscout-source`, name 'Nightscout Data Source', version '1.0.0', apiVersion PLUGIN_API_VERSION, description 'Cloud-mediated: pulls glucose & insulin from your Nightscout connection.', author 'GlycemicGPT', protocolName 'Nightscout'.
capabilities = {DATA_SYNC} ONLY (MULTI_INSTANCE) so enabling it NEVER evicts a BLE pump's glucose/insulin/pump-status slots (AC5). `getCapability()` always returns null.

Lifecycle: `initialize(context)` is intentionally EMPTY and intentionally does NOT use `context.settingsStore` — because the WorkManager worker is constructed by HiltWorkerFactory outside the plugin's lifecycle and cannot receive a PluginContext; instead the worker, plugin and manager all share one Hilt-injected `NightscoutSyncStore`, itself backed by the SAME `PluginSettingsStoreImpl(PLUGIN_ID)` file the platform hands the plugin. `shutdown()` is empty (reserved for runtime-plugin removal, which doesn't apply). `onActivated()` → `syncManager.enable()`. `onDeactivated()` → `syncManager.disable()`. Off by default (AC1); deactivating stops the schedule but KEEPS cached Room data (AC8).

`settingsDescriptor()` = one section 'Nightscout' with one InfoText key `cloud_mediated_note`: 'Cloud-mediated: when enabled, your Nightscout data is pulled from your GlycemicGPT account on this device. Requires a Nightscout connection set up on your account.'

`observeDashboardCards()` = `store.state.map { listOf(buildCard(it)) }`. Card: id `nightscout_sync`, title 'Nightscout', priority 200, hasDetail = true, elements = [IconValue(SYNC, 'Cloud source'), Label(formatLastSync(lastSuccessAtMs), CAPTION), optional StatusBadge].
`formatLastSync(null)` = 'Not synced yet'; else `"Last sync: " + DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMM d, HH:mm").withZone(ZoneId.systemDefault())`.
`statusBadge(status)`: OK/NEVER → null (nothing worth flagging); NO_CONNECTION → StatusBadge('No active Nightscout connection', WARNING); AUTH_ERROR → StatusBadge('Reconnect needed', ERROR); ERROR → StatusBadge('Sync error — will retry', WARNING).

`observeDetailScreen(cardId)`: returns null unless cardId == `nightscout_sync`. Otherwise a flow that loads the connection list ONCE when the screen opens, then `emitAll(store.state.map { buildDetailScreen(connections, it) })` so the UI re-renders reactively on every sync-state change and never goes stale after a 'Sync now' tap. `loadActiveConnections()` = `connectionsProvider().filter { it.isActive }` inside try/catch → emptyList on failure (warn logged).
Detail elements: SectionHeader('Nightscout sync'); Display(Label(formatLastSync, BODY)); optional Display(statusBadge); Interactive(Dropdown(key = `selected_connection_id`, label 'Connection', options = active connections as (id, name))) ONLY when `activeConnections.size > 1` ('only offer a picker when there is an actual choice to make'); Interactive(ActionButton(key `sync_now`, label 'Sync now', PRIMARY)). Title 'Nightscout'.
`onDetailAction(cardId, actionKey)`: `if (cardId == CARD_ID && actionKey == "sync_now") syncManager.syncNow()`.

`NightscoutSourceFactory` (@Singleton, @Inject) binds via `NightscoutSourceModule` (@Binds @IntoSet). Its `connectionsProvider` = `api.listNightscoutConnections()` returning `body()?.connections ?: emptyList()` on success and emptyList on any non-2xx.
edge_cases: The connection dropdown writes directly to the plugin's SharedPreferences via the generic settings renderer — the plugin itself never observes the write; the sync engine reads it on the next run.
The connection list is fetched once per detail-screen open; a connection added/removed while the screen is open is not reflected.
In BLE-only mode (no backend), Settings hides the Activate control entirely (see Settings capability).

capabilities.name: NightscoutSyncManager (WorkManager scheduling)
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton class NightscoutSyncManager(@ApplicationContext context, store: NightscoutSyncStore, authTokenStore: AuthTokenStore)`.
Constants: `PERIODIC_WORK = "nightscout_source_periodic_sync"`, `ONESHOT_WORK = "nightscout_source_oneshot_sync"`, `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 15L`.

`enable()`: `store.enabled = true`; if `standDownWithoutBackend("enable")` returns true → RETURN (flag still persisted); else `enqueuePeriodic()` then `syncNow()`; log 'Nightscout-source sync enabled'.
`disable()`: `store.enabled = false`; `WorkManager.cancelUniqueWork(PERIODIC_WORK)` (the one-shot is NOT cancelled here); log 'Nightscout-source sync disabled (cached data retained)'.
`syncNow()`: if standDownWithoutBackend → return; else enqueue a `OneTimeWorkRequest<NightscoutSyncWorker>` with the network constraint under `ONESHOT_WORK` with `ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE`.
`standDownWithoutBackend(caller)`: returns false if `authTokenStore.isBackendConfigured()`; otherwise cancels BOTH unique works (so a schedule left from a previous full-stack life cannot keep waking a sync that can never succeed), logs 'Nightscout-source %s skipped: no backend configured', returns true.
`enqueuePeriodic()`: `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<NightscoutSyncWorker>(15, TimeUnit.MINUTES)` with the network constraint, `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(PERIODIC_WORK, ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE, request)`.
Network constraint (both request types): `Constraints.Builder().setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED).build()` (AC6) — offline simply leaves the last-cached data in place.

Cadence rationale in-code: WorkManager's periodic floor is 15 minutes; each run fully backfills everything since the cursor, so a faster Nightscout upload interval never LOSES data — it only changes freshness (AC3).
The activation flag persists across the stand-down, so sync resumes when a backend (re)appears and the plugin is restored or re-enabled.
`isBackendConfigured()` = a non-blank base URL is stored in AuthTokenStore; when absent, BaseUrlInterceptor refuses every request.
edge_cases: `disable()` cancels only the periodic work; an in-flight one-shot can still run, but the engine's `store.enabled` check makes it a no-op (SyncOutcome.Disabled).
ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE means re-enabling updates the existing schedule rather than restarting its interval.

capabilities.name: NightscoutSyncEngine (pull, paging, cursor, outcome classification)
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton class NightscoutSyncEngine(api: GlycemicGptApi, pumpDao: PumpDao, store: NightscoutSyncStore, authTokenStore: AuthTokenStore)`. Pure logic extracted from the worker so it is unit-testable without an Android/WorkManager harness. `PAGE_LIMIT = 500` (matches the backend's default `limit`).

`sealed interface SyncOutcome`: `Disabled`, `NoBackend`, `NoConnection`, `Success(pages, cgm, bolus, basal)` (row counts written, post-mapping/pre-dedupe), `AuthError`, `Transient`.

`syncOnce(nowMs = System.currentTimeMillis())`:
1. `if (!store.enabled) return Disabled`.
2. `if (!authTokenStore.isBackendConfigured()) return NoBackend` — a BLE-only BACKSTOP. NO status is recorded ('no server at all is a mode, not a sync failure of this plugin'). Without it, an in-flight periodic run racing the mode flip would hit BaseUrlInterceptor's IOException, be classified Transient, and retry forever on a condition only the user can resolve.
3. `api.listNightscoutConnections().bodyOrThrow().connections` → `resolveConnection(...)`; null → `store.recordStatus(NO_CONNECTION)` + return NoConnection.
4. `runSync(connection, nowMs)` (records success internally).
Catch order: `SyncAuthError` → warn 'gave up (http %d)', `recordStatus(AUTH_ERROR)`, return AuthError; `SyncTransientError` → warn, `recordStatus(ERROR)`, return Transient; `IOException` → warn, `recordStatus(ERROR)`, return Transient.

`bodyOrThrow()`: successful with null body → `SyncTransientError("empty body")`; HTTP 401/403/404 → `SyncAuthError(code)`; any other non-2xx → `SyncTransientError("http <code>")`.

`resolveConnection(connections)`: filter isActive; if `store.selectedConnectionId` is non-empty → `active.firstOrNull { it.id == selectedId }` (returns NULL if the selection was deleted/deactivated — deliberately surfaced as NO_CONNECTION rather than SILENTLY SYNCING A DIFFERENT CONNECTION into the same tables); else `active.firstOrNull()`.

`runSync` paging loop (per-connection cursor, INCLUSIVE `since`):
- `cursorMs = store.getCursor(connection.id)`; `sinceIso = if (cursorMs > 0) Instant.ofEpochMilli(cursorMs).toString() else null`.
- `api.getNightscoutData(connection.id, sinceIso, 500).bodyOrThrow()`; pages++.
- If BOTH `glucoseReadings` and `pumpEvents` are empty → break.
- Map via NightscoutDataMapper and insert each non-empty batch (`insertCgmBatch`, `insertBoluses`, `insertBasalBatch`); accumulate counts.
- `effLimit = data.effectiveLimitPerArray.coerceAtLeast(1)`; `glucoseFull = glucoseReadings.size >= effLimit`; `eventsFull = pumpEvents.size >= effLimit`.
- `glucoseMax` / `eventsMax` = max epoch ms in each array; `overallMax = maxOf(cursorMs, glucoseMax ?: cursorMs, eventsMax ?: cursorMs)`.
- If NEITHER array is full → both streams fully drained: `cursorMs = overallMax`, break.
- Otherwise (asymmetric truncation): the backend pages each array independently as `ts >= since ORDER BY ts ASC LIMIT n`, so a SHORT array is fully drained for this `since` and only a FULL array may have more rows. Advance only as far as the lagging FULL stream so its un-fetched tail is never skipped: `next = listOfNotNull(glucoseMax.takeIf { glucoseFull }, eventsMax.takeIf { eventsFull }).minOrNull() ?: overallMax`. The other stream's re-fetched boundary rows are harmless (idempotent inserts).
- CURSOR-STALL GUARD: `if (next <= cursorMs)` → `store.setCursor(connection.id, cursorMs)` (persist progress made) then `throw SyncTransientError("cursor stalled at $cursorMs on a saturated boundary page")` — surfaces a RETRYABLE error instead of a false success that would silently drop the un-fetched tail. In-code note: unreachable with real CGM data (would need >500 rows sharing a single millisecond).
- Else `cursorMs = next`, loop.
On normal exit: `store.setCursor(connection.id, cursorMs)`, `store.recordSuccess(nowMs)`, `Timber.i("Nightscout sync ok: pages=%d cgm=%d bolus=%d basal=%d")`, return Success.

DEDUPE DESIGN DECISION: the `since` cursor is INCLUSIVE, so idempotent DAO inserts (unique `timestampMs` for cgm/basal, unique `(units, timestampMs)` for bolus) absorb the boundary-row duplicates the backend warns about — THERE IS NO SEPARATE ns_id DEDUPE PASS (the `ns_id` field exists in the DTO but is unused by the mapper).

PHI LOGGING RULE (explicit): 'Logging is row counts + HTTP status only -- never glucose/insulin values or connection credentials (PHI).'
edge_cases: The paging loop has NO iteration cap — a pathological backend could loop indefinitely; only the cursor-stall guard breaks a non-advancing loop.
Cursor 0 means full backfill (since = null).
A cursor is per-connection (`last_sync_cursor_ms.<connectionId>`), so switching connections starts a fresh backfill for the new one and preserves the old one's cursor.
The whole sync runs inside WorkManager's doWork with no explicit timeout.

capabilities.name: NightscoutSyncStore (typed plugin persistence + reactive state)
capabilities.behavior:
`class NightscoutSyncStore(store: PluginSettingsStore)` — provided as a @Singleton by NightscoutSourceModule as `NightscoutSyncStore(PluginSettingsStoreImpl(context, NightscoutSourcePlugin.PLUGIN_ID))`, keying it to the SAME SharedPreferences file the platform hands the plugin, so the detail-screen dropdown's writes are visible to the worker.

Keys: `enabled` (Boolean, default false), `selected_connection_id` (String, default ""), `last_sync_cursor_ms.<connectionId>` (String-encoded Long), `last_sync_at_ms` (String-encoded Long), `last_sync_status` (String enum name). Longs are stored as Strings because PluginSettingsStore has no long accessor.

`enum NightscoutSyncStatus { NEVER, OK, NO_CONNECTION, AUTH_ERROR, ERROR }`.
`data class NightscoutSyncState(status, lastSuccessAtMs: Long?)`.
`getCursor(connectionId)` = `store.getString(key, "0").toLongOrNull() ?: 0L`.
`recordSuccess(nowMs)`: writes status=OK and last_sync_at_ms=nowMs, sets `_state.value = NightscoutSyncState(OK, nowMs)`.
`recordStatus(status)`: writes the status only and does `_state.value = _state.value.copy(status = status)` — DELIBERATELY PRESERVING the last SUCCESSFUL sync timestamp.
`readState()` (initial): `runCatching { NightscoutSyncStatus.valueOf(store.getString(KEY_STATUS, "")) }.getOrDefault(NEVER)` plus `last_sync_at_ms.toLongOrNull()`.
`state: StateFlow<NightscoutSyncState>` drives the dashboard card's last-sync line and error badge.
edge_cases: The StateFlow is in-memory per singleton; the persisted status is re-read only at construction.
Cursors are never cleaned up when a connection is deleted — the key lingers in SharedPreferences.
`recordStatus` intentionally does NOT clear lastSuccessAtMs, so the card can show 'Last sync: <old time>' alongside 'Reconnect needed'.

capabilities.name: NightscoutSyncWorker (WorkManager shell)
capabilities.behavior:
`@HiltWorker class NightscoutSyncWorker @AssistedInject constructor(@Assisted context, @Assisted params, engine: NightscoutSyncEngine) : CoroutineWorker`. Deliberately thin: all logic lives in the engine.
`doWork()`: calls `engine.syncOnce()` inside try/catch. `CancellationException` is RETHROWN (cooperative cancellation, e.g. WorkManager stopping the work, must propagate rather than be swallowed into a retry). Any other Exception → `Timber.e(e, "Nightscout sync worker crashed; will retry")` + `Result.retry()`.
Outcome mapping: `if (outcome is SyncOutcome.Transient) Result.retry() else Result.success()`. So Disabled, NoBackend, NoConnection, Success and AuthError all yield `Result.success()` — i.e. NoBackend and AuthError are TERMINAL for the run (retrying cannot help until the user acts). Retry backoff is WorkManager's default (exponential, 30s initial, capped) — no custom backoff policy is set.
edge_cases: The worker never returns Result.failure() — it can only succeed or retry, so a chained work sequence is never broken.

capabilities.name: NightscoutDataMapper (ingestion validation and source attribution)
capabilities.behavior:
`object NightscoutDataMapper` — pure/synchronous, unit-testable without Android. `const val SOURCE = "nightscout-source"` is stamped on every row (cgm_readings, basal_readings and bolus_events all have a `source` column).

Bounds:
- `GLUCOSE_RANGE = CgmReading.MIN_MG_DL..CgmReading.MAX_MG_DL` = 20..500.
- `BOLUS_RANGE = 0f..BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS` = 0f..25f.
- `MAX_BASAL_RATE_U_HR = SafetyLimits.ABSOLUTE_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS / 1000f` = 15.0 U/hr — the ONLY unit conversion in this subsystem (milliunits → units, divide by 1000).

`toCgmEntities(data)`: `glucoseReadings.filter { it.value in 20..500 }.map { CgmReadingEntity(glucoseMgDl = r.value, trendArrow = r.trend, source = SOURCE, timestampMs = r.readingTimestamp.toEpochMilli()) }`.
`toBolusEntities(data)`: `pumpEvents.filter { it.eventType in BOLUS_TYPES && it.units != null && it.units in 0f..25f }` where `BOLUS_TYPES = setOf("bolus", "correction")`. Maps to `BolusEventEntity(units, isAutomated = e.isAutomated || isCorrection, isCorrection = (eventType == "correction"), source = SOURCE, timestampMs = e.eventTimestamp.toEpochMilli())`. Rationale: a `correction` is by definition an automated (Control-IQ-style) correction in the platform taxonomy, so it is automated regardless of the upload's flag; user-initiated doses arrive as `bolus`.
`toBasalEntities(data)`: `pumpEvents.filter { it.eventType == "basal" && it.units != null && it.units in 0f..15f }` → `BasalReadingEntity(rate = e.units!!, isAutomated = e.isAutomated, activityMode = "", source = SOURCE, timestampMs = ...)`. In-code note: `in 0f..MAX` ALSO REJECTS NaN/Infinity (out-of-range float comparisons are false). activityMode is blank because Nightscout basal events carry no pump activity mode (sleep/exercise), matching how BLE writers leave unobserved fields.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSION: `combo_bolus` is EXCLUDED from BOLUS_TYPES. Rationale in-code: the backend taxonomy uses it for either a real combo bolus or an AAPS extendedEmulated temp-basal-rate whose `units` is the EXTENDED PORTION rather than a point-in-time dose — counting it would INFLATE bolus totals / IoB. Left out until its semantics are validated.

VALIDATION RATIONALE (explicit): out-of-range values from the backend are DROPPED at this ingestion boundary rather than throwing (which would abort a whole page), so the local DB never stores physiologically impossible readings; without it such rows would be written and then silently discarded again when the entity is mapped back to its domain model on read.

CROSS-SOURCE COEXISTENCE (explicit): a Nightscout row and a BLE row at the same timestamp collapse to ONE row via the unique indexes — `cgm_readings(timestampMs)` unique, `basal_readings(timestampMs)` unique, `bolus_events(units, timestampMs)` unique. Which row wins depends on the DAO conflict strategy: `insertCgmBatch` and `insertBasalBatch` use `OnConflictStrategy.IGNORE` (existing row wins — FIRST writer), `insertBoluses` uses `OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE` (new row wins — LAST writer). Either way there is no double-counting.
edge_cases: The mapper filters against ABSOLUTE bounds, NOT the user's narrower SafetyLimits — a user-configured max of e.g. 400 mg/dL does not filter Nightscout ingestion.
Two DIFFERENT boluses with different unit amounts at the exact same millisecond both persist (the unique index includes units).
Dropped rows are silent — no counter, no log of what was rejected (deliberate PHI-logging policy).
