BasalReadingEntity.activityMode is a String "" here, while the domain model uses the PumpActivityMode enum — the entity→domain mapping must tolerate an empty string.

capabilities.name: Nightscout DTOs and backend endpoints
capabilities.behavior:
Moshi DTOs in `data/remote/dto/NightscoutDtos.kt`, mirroring the backend's `NightscoutDataResponse` family (`apps/api/src/schemas/nightscout.py`):
- `NightscoutConnectionDto(id: String, name: String, @Json("is_active") isActive: Boolean = true)`
- `NightscoutConnectionListDto(connections: List<NightscoutConnectionDto>)` — the backend returns `{"connections": [...]}`, NOT a bare array.
- `NightscoutGlucoseReadingDto(@Json("ns_id") nsId: String? = null, @Json("reading_timestamp") readingTimestamp: Instant, value: Int, trend: String, @Json("trend_rate") trendRate: Float? = null, source: String)`
- `NightscoutPumpEventDto(@Json("ns_id") nsId: String? = null, @Json("event_timestamp") eventTimestamp: Instant, @Json("event_type") eventType: String, units: Float? = null, @Json("duration_minutes") durationMinutes: Int? = null, @Json("is_automated") isAutomated: Boolean = false, source: String)`
- `NightscoutDataDto(@Json("connection_id") connectionId: String, @Json("fetched_at") fetchedAt: Instant, @Json("effective_limit_per_array") effectiveLimitPerArray: Int, @Json("glucose_readings") …, @Json("pump_events") …)`

Retrofit (GlycemicGptApi):
- `@GET("/api/integrations/nightscout") suspend fun listNightscoutConnections(): Response<NightscoutConnectionListDto>`
- `@GET("/api/integrations/nightscout/{connectionId}/data") suspend fun getNightscoutData(@Path("connectionId") connectionId: String, @Query("since") since: String?, @Query("limit") limit: Int): Response<NightscoutDataDto>` — `since` is an ISO-8601 Instant string (`Instant.toString()`), `limit` is always 500.
Also plugin-related: `@PUT("/api/settings/plugin-declarations")` and `@DELETE("/api/settings/plugin-declarations")`.

Fields present but UNUSED by the mapper today: `nsId`, `trendRate`, `durationMinutes`, `source` (the DTO's own source is discarded in favor of the constant "nightscout-source"), `connectionId`, `fetchedAt`.
edge_cases: `durationMinutes` is dropped, so a temp-basal's duration is lost — the basal row is a point-in-time rate only.
`effectiveLimitPerArray` is the backend's authoritative per-array page size and drives the truncation detection; the client's requested `limit=500` is only a hint.

capabilities.name: Plugin declaration sync to backend (bolus categories)
capabilities.behavior:
`HomeViewModel.syncPluginDeclaration(plugin: DevicePlugin?)`, called on active-pump changes. Logic:
- plugin == null → `api.deletePluginDeclarations()`; success or HTTP 404 → 'Plugin declaration cleared'; else warn with the HTTP code.
- `plugin.asBolusCategoryProvider()` == null → DELETE, 'Plugin declaration cleared (no bolus category provider)'.
- `provider.declaredCategories()` empty → DELETE, 'Plugin declaration cleared (empty declared categories)'.
- Otherwise build `mappings = declared.associate { it to provider.toPlatformCategory(it) }` skipping nulls, and PUT `PluginDeclarationRequest(@Json("plugin_id") pluginId, @Json("plugin_name") pluginName, @Json("plugin_version") pluginVersion, @Json("declared_categories") declaredCategories: List<String>, @Json("category_mappings") categoryMappings: Map<String,String>)`.
Whole function wrapped in try/catch(Exception) → `Timber.w(e, "Failed to sync plugin declaration")`.

Related read path: `HomeViewModel.pumpLabelMap: StateFlow<Map<BolusCategory, String>?>` builds the REVERSE map (platform category → pump-native label) from the active plugin's BolusCategoryProvider, returning null when there's no plugin/provider or nothing declared, in try/catch (warn + null). Consumed only when the debug 'Show Pump Labels' toggle is enabled.
edge_cases: HTTP 404 on DELETE is treated as success (nothing to clear).

capabilities.name: Community contributor path (what shipping a driver requires today)
capabilities.behavior:
TWO paths.

COMPILE-TIME (the endorsed path, per CONTRIBUTING.md §Device Data Drivers):
1. Pick a device that isn't already supported.
2. Open an issue describing the device, the protocol, and the data to surface.
3. Submit a PR with a new Gradle module under `plugins/shipped/<device-name>/` (these ARE compiled into official builds), declaring ONLY capabilities from the official read-only enum (typical: GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BGM_SOURCE, CALIBRATION_TARGET, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER).
4. Include unit tests, especially for parsing and SafetyLimits validation of incoming values.
5. Use the existing plugins as reference implementations.
Mechanics: `build.gradle.kts` applying com.android.library + kotlin.android + hilt + ksp, depending on `project(":pump-driver-api")` plus hilt/coroutines FROM THE VERSION CATALOG (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`) — 'Do not hardcode version strings'; register in `settings.gradle.kts` with an explicit `projectDir`; add as a dependency of `:app`; provide a `@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class) abstract class XModule { @Binds @IntoSet abstract fun bindXFactory(impl: XPluginFactory): PluginFactory }`; factory is `@Singleton` with an `@Inject` constructor and can take DI dependencies.
Reference layout (Tandem): plugin/TandemDevicePlugin.kt, TandemPluginFactory.kt, TandemGlucoseSource.kt, TandemInsulinSource.kt, TandemPumpStatus.kt, TandemBolusCategoryProvider.kt, di/TandemPumpModule.kt. Capability classes are THIN delegates over the BLE layer — e.g. TandemGlucoseSource.observeReadings() is `flow { while (true) { bleDriver.getCgmStatus().onSuccess { emit(it) }; delay(60_000L) } }` (POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000L; Medtronic uses the identical 60_000L cadence, with a comment that cadence ownership moves to the polling orchestrator in Milestone D).

RUNTIME (advanced, NOT compiled into official builds):
1. Kotlin/Java project depending on `pump-driver-api` COMPILE-ONLY (extract classes.jar from the AAR into `libs/`, or `compileOnly(project(":pump-driver-api"))` inside the monorepo). Also `compileOnly("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.10.2")`. Plain `kotlin("jvm")`, JVM target 17.
2. Implement `PluginFactory` with a NO-ARG constructor (factories are reflected — NO dependency injection available) and `Plugin`.
3. Add `src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.json`.
4. `./gradlew jar` → `d8 --output dex-out/ build/libs/example-plugin.jar` → `cp build/libs/example-plugin.jar example-plugin.jar` → `jar uf example-plugin.jar -C dex-out classes.dex`.

Compile-time vs runtime (documented table): discovery = Hilt @IntoSet vs DexClassLoader+manifest; Context = full vs RestrictedContext; credentials = full PumpCredentialProvider vs per-plugin ScopedCredentialProvider; safety limits, event bus and settings store identical; removable = No vs Yes; shipped in APK = Yes vs No.

Runtime factories cannot use DI, so all their dependencies must be constructed inside the plugin from the PluginContext.

capabilities.behavior:
TANDEM (`:tandem-pump-driver`, plugins/shipped/tandem, id `com.glycemicgpt.tandem`, name 'Tandem Insulin Pump', v1.0.0, protocolName 'Tandem', description 'Tandem insulin pumps (t:slim X2, Mobi) with Dexcom CGM'): capabilities = {GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER}. initialize() = no-op (BLE components injected ready-to-use); shutdown() = connectionManager.disconnect(); onActivated() = connectionManager.autoReconnectIfPaired(); onDeactivated() = connectionManager.disconnect(). connect(address, config) → `connectionManager.connect(address, config["pairingCode"])`. scan() maps BleScanner's DiscoveredPump → DiscoveredDevice stamped with PLUGIN_ID. settingsDescriptor() = EMPTY sections ('the generic pump settings card already renders live pairing status and the Unpair action'). observeDashboardCards() = flowOf(emptyList()). Pairing style: default CENTRAL_SCAN.

MEDTRONIC (`:medtronic-pump-driver`, plugins/shipped/medtronic, id = MedtronicBleConnectionManager.PLUGIN_ID, name 'Medtronic MiniMed Pump', v1.0.0, protocolName 'Medtronic', description 'Medtronic MiniMed 700-series pumps (680G / 770G / 780G) over Bluetooth (read-only, BETA)'): capabilities = {GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS}. File header states READ-ONLY explicitly: 'there is no PUMP_CONTROL capability in the platform and no method here writes to the pump.' shutdown() calls `connectionManager.close()` (full teardown of worker thread + coroutine scope) while onDeactivated() calls only `disconnect()` — the distinction is documented: close() is reserved for terminal shutdown so the plugin can be reactivated after deactivation. onActivated() = reconnectIfPaired(). pairingProfile = ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT with advertisedName = MedtronicBleConnectionManager.DEFAULT_LOCAL_NAME. observePairingFault() maps MedtronicConnectionFault → PairingFault (PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED, ADVERTISE_FAILED, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, AUTH_FAILED, BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED→BOUND_ELSEWHERE). connect() ignores `address` and calls `startSession(forceFirstPair = config["forceFirstPair"].toBoolean())`. settingsDescriptor() contributes ONE InfoText (key `single_peer_note`): 'A MiniMed pump pairs with only one phone at a time. Remove the pump from the official Medtronic app before pairing it here.' Gated by BuildConfig.MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED.
MedtronicInsulinSource.getBolusHistory uses a `Mutex` + a process-local `bolusCursor: Int?` sequence cursor; the whole read-fetch-advance runs under the mutex so concurrent calls cannot regress the cursor or fetch overlapping windows; over-cap boluses are 'dropped, not clamped'; the slow loop's raw-history sync is the durable, self-healing bolus path (it persists each raw HistoryLogRecord keyed by sequence before advancing its own cursor).
edge_cases: Neither shipped driver contributes dashboard cards — the only plugin card in the app today is Nightscout's.
Both drivers' GlucoseSource.observeReadings() are infinite `while(true)` polling flows at 60_000 ms with no jitter or backoff; failures are swallowed by `onSuccess`.

safety_critical: GLUCOSE VALIDATION BOUNDS — 20..500 mg/dL, enforced in FIVE independent places that must all be reproduced: CgmReading init `require(glucoseMgDl in MIN_MG_DL..MAX_MG_DL)` (20/500); BgmReading init `require(glucoseMgDl in 20..500)`; PluginEvent.CalibrationRequested init `require(bgValueMgDl in 20..500)`; CalibrationTarget.validateBgValue() returning Result.failure outside ABSOLUTE_MIN_GLUCOSE..ABSOLUTE_MAX_GLUCOSE; NightscoutDataMapper.GLUCOSE_RANGE filter. Constructing an out-of-range reading THROWS — so a port that silently clamps instead of throwing changes failure semantics from 'driver crashes loudly' to 'wrong number on a glucose chart'.

SAFETY LIMITS ARE NARROW-ONLY, NEVER WIDENABLE — SafetyLimits.init hard-requires min>=20, max<=500, maxBasal in 1..15_000 mU/hr, maxBolus in 1..25_000 mU. `safeOf()` clamps rather than throws and is the ONLY path used for backend-supplied values (SafetyLimitsStore.updateAll clamps before persisting AND toSafetyLimits() clamps again on read). A port must preserve both the strict constructor (programmatic callers) and the lenient clamping factory (external data), and must never allow a backend value to widen the absolute bounds.

DROP, NEVER CLAMP — PumpStatus.extractCgmFromHistoryLogs / extractBolusesFromHistoryLogs / extractBasalFromHistoryLogs and InsulinSource.getBolusHistory all receive SafetyLimits and are contractually required to DISCARD out-of-range records, not clamp them. This is convention + unit tests only; the interfaces do not enforce it. Clamping would silently fabricate a plausible-looking dose or glucose value.

INSULIN DOSE DISPLAY BOUNDS — BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f is a hard `require` on units, correctionUnits and mealUnits (all must be >=0 and <=25). BasalReading has no init guard; the only basal ceiling is 15 U/hr, applied at the Nightscout ingestion boundary via ABSOLUTE_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS/1000f. A ported BasalReading with no ceiling would accept an arbitrary rate from a driver.

UNIT CONVERSION — the ONLY conversion in this subsystem is milliunits→units, `SafetyLimits.ABSOLUTE_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS / 1000f` = 15.0 U/hr in NightscoutDataMapper. SafetyLimits speaks MILLIUNITS (15_000 / 25_000); BolusEvent/BasalReading speak FLOAT UNITS (25f / 15f). Mixing the two by a factor of 1000 in a port would either reject everything or accept a 25,000 U bolus. Glucose is mg/dL end-to-end with NO conversion anywhere in this subsystem.

NightscoutDataMapper drops NaN/Infinity implicitly — `it.units in 0f..MAX_BASAL_RATE_U_HR` is false for NaN and Infinity because out-of-range float comparisons are false. A Swift port using `abs()`/optional comparisons must add explicit `isFinite` checks or NaN will pass.

combo_bolus IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from Nightscout bolus ingestion — including it would count an AAPS extendedEmulated temp-basal's extended portion as a point-in-time dose, INFLATING bolus totals and IoB. Reproducing the mapper without this exclusion directly corrupts insulin totals shown to the patient.

`correction` events are forced to isAutomated = true regardless of the upload's flag (a correction is by definition an automated Control-IQ-style correction in the platform taxonomy). Getting this wrong misattributes automated insulin as user-delivered.

STALENESS IS TIMESTAMP-BASED AND SOURCE-AGNOSTIC — NightscoutDataMapper stores the reading's REAL capture timestamp (`readingTimestamp`), NOT the sync/fetch time. This is pinned by NightscoutCgmFreshnessTest and is what makes a frozen Nightscout feed age out identically to a frozen BLE feed. FreshnessPolicy.CGM = staleAfterMs 6 min, tooStaleAfterMs 15 min (half-open bounds); the on-device alert floor fires ONLY on FRESH. Stamping sync time instead would make a dead feed look permanently live.

EVENT BUS HAS NO DELIVERY GUARANTEE — MutableSharedFlow(extraBufferCapacity = 256, onBufferOverflow = DROP_OLDEST, replay = 0). Overflow silently drops the OLDEST event with only a Timber warning; late subscribers see nothing. A CalibrationRequested event can be dropped. Nothing safety-critical currently depends on the bus, but any port that routes alerts or calibration through it inherits an at-most-once, lossy channel.

SafetyLimitsChanged is PLATFORM-ONLY — PluginEventBusImpl.publish() silently drops it (warning only, no exception) when a plugin attempts it; only the `internal` publishPlatform() can emit it. A plugin able to forge SafetyLimitsChanged could convince other plugins to accept out-of-range data.

NO THERAPEUTIC WRITE SURFACE — stated in three places (docs, CONTRIBUTING.md, MedtronicDevicePlugin header) as a deliberate architectural decision: no bolus dosing, no basal-rate change, no pump-setting write. calibrate()/unpair()/autoReconnectIfPaired()/connect()/disconnect() are classified as session/lifecycle, not therapy. Capability enforcement at the registry boundary (refusing plugins declaring capabilities outside the official enum) is documented as PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — today a runtime plugin's declared capability set is trusted.

RUNTIME PLUGIN SANDBOX IS IN-PROCESS ONLY — DexClassLoader with the app's classloader as parent means a runtime plugin can reflect over host app classes; RestrictedContext is a language-level ContextWrapper, not process isolation. Documented and accepted. Runtime plugin credentials use PLAIN SharedPreferences (not EncryptedSharedPreferences) because plugins cannot access AndroidX Security — readable via run-as on rooted/debug devices, documented as accepted for the current trust model.

HistoryLogParserAdapter returns emptyList() (not an error) when no plugin is active — a caller cannot distinguish 'no history records' from 'no driver installed'. In a port this must not be mistaken for 'the patient had no boluses'.

PHI LOGGING RULE — NightscoutSyncEngine logs row counts and HTTP status ONLY, never glucose/insulin values or connection credentials. DebugLogger's interface doc requires raw packet data (cargoHex, parsedValue — which may contain glucose readings, insulin doses, device identifiers) be retained only in debug builds and never persisted unencrypted.

Cross-source write collisions are resolved by DIFFERENT conflict strategies per table: cgm_readings and basal_readings use IGNORE (first writer wins), bolus_events uses REPLACE (last writer wins). A port that unifies these changes which value the patient sees when a Nightscout row and a BLE row land on the same timestamp.

Nightscout ingestion filters against ABSOLUTE bounds (20..500, 0..25 U, 0..15 U/hr) and NOT against the user's narrower configured SafetyLimits — a deliberate asymmetry with the BLE extract* path, which does receive the user's limits.

map.notes:
DOC DRIFT FOUND (the doc is authoritative on intent, the code on behavior — the code wins):
1. docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md says PLUGIN_API_VERSION is `2` (in both the API Versioning and Manifest sections). The code says `5` (PluginMetadata.kt), with an in-file changelog: v3 = BasalReading.controlIqMode→activityMode (PumpActivityMode enum), v4 = BolusEvent.category + BolusCategoryProvider, v5 = getFullHistoryLogs() on PumpDriver/PumpStatus.
2. plugins/example/src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.json declares `"apiVersion": 1` and its README says "currently 1". Because DexPluginLoader enforces EXACT equality with PLUGIN_API_VERSION=5, the shipped reference plugin JAR would be REJECTED today. The Kotlin factory uses the constant, so only the JSON manifest and README are stale.
3. The docs' capability table lists 6 capabilities and omits BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER entirely; the enum has 7. The docs also omit `getFullHistoryLogs`, `PairingProfile`/`PairingFault`/`observePairingFault`, `observeDetailScreen`/`onDetailAction`, and the DetailScreenDescriptor/DetailElement types.
4. The docs describe `shutdown()` as "not currently called by the registry"; that is true for compile-time plugins but `removeRuntimePlugin` DOES call it.
5. The docs' PluginMetadata signature omits default values; the real data class defaults description/author to "" and iconResName/protocolName to null.
6. The docs describe the DATA_SYNC capability as "not yet defined ... not currently implementable" — it is in fact used today by both NightscoutSourcePlugin and the example plugin as a pure activation tag (it still has no capability interface).

EXPLICIT DESIGN DECISIONS TO CARRY INTO THE PORT (each has an in-code rationale):
- Activate-new-before-deactivate-old so a single-instance capability slot is never empty.
- Reserve the compile-time plugin ID in `compileTimePluginIds` BEFORE calling create(), so a runtime plugin cannot hijack a built-in ID if the built-in's init fails transiently.
- A feature-gated-off plugin's persisted activation preference is deliberately left untouched, so re-enabling restores the user's prior selection.
- Runtime plugin sandboxing is by ALLOWLIST for hardware services and BLOCKLIST for app-scope escapes, with the stated philosophy "safety enforcement comes from SafetyLimits, not from blanket Context restrictions."
- Full process isolation for runtime plugins was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED as too complex; the trust model (explicit user install + red warning) is the mitigation.
- EncryptedSharedPreferences for runtime plugin credentials was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED (plugins can't reach AndroidX Security); the residual risk is documented.
- Nightscout dedupe is by INCLUSIVE cursor + unique DB indexes, NOT by ns_id — there is deliberately no ns_id dedupe pass.
- The Nightscout cursor advances only as far as the LAGGING FULL stream on asymmetric truncation, and a saturated-boundary page raises a retryable Transient error rather than a false success.
- NoBackend is a terminal, status-free outcome ("no server at all is a mode, not a sync failure of this plugin") specifically to avoid an infinite retry loop only the user can resolve.
- combo_bolus excluded from bolus ingestion until its semantics are validated.
- Nightscout activation is hidden in Settings when no backend is configured, derived from state rather than filtered at mutation sites so it can never go stale.

PORTING GAPS TO FLAG (mechanism, not iOS advice — a separate pass owns that):
- The entire runtime-plugin path (DexClassLoader, JAR install, RestrictedContext, ScopedCredentialProvider, PluginFileManager, PluginManifest, the Custom Plugins UI) is built on Android's ability to load code at runtime. That mechanism has no equivalent on the target platform.
- Hilt `@IntoSet` multibinding is how compile-time plugins are discovered; there is no runtime registration API — a port needs an explicit registration mechanism.
- Nothing in this subsystem is Wear-specific; plugin cards/detail screens are phone-only surfaces today.

TEST COVERAGE THAT PINS BEHAVIOR (useful as a port acceptance suite): app/src/test/.../plugin/{PluginRegistryTest, DexPluginLoaderTest, PluginFileManagerTest, PluginManifestTest, PluginEventBusImplTest, RestrictedPluginContextTest} and .../plugin/nightscout/{NightscoutSyncEngineTest, NightscoutSyncManagerTest, NightscoutSyncWorkerTest, NightscoutDataMapperTest, NightscoutSourcePluginTest, NightscoutCgmFreshnessTest}; plus pump-driver-api/src/test/.../{SafetyLimitsTest, SettingDescriptorTest, DashboardCardDescriptorTest, DetailScreenDescriptorTest}.

ports_cleanly.capability: Plugin interface and lifecycle contract (metadata, capabilities, initialize/shutdown/onActivated/onDeactivated, settingsDescriptor, observeDashboardCards, getCapability, observeDetailScreen/onDetailAction)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A Swift `protocol GlucoseDriver`-style `Plugin` protocol in a `DriverAPI` SPM target. `Flow<T>` -> `AsyncStream<T>`; `StateFlow<T>` -> an `@Observable`/`AsyncStream` pair with a synchronous `current` accessor (StateFlow's always-has-a-value semantic is load-bearing for `safetyLimits`). `suspend fun ... : Result<T>` -> `async throws`. Default interface members -> protocol extension defaults (`observeDetailScreen` returns nil, `onDetailAction` no-ops). Lifecycle serialization (`synchronized(activationLock)`) -> make the registry an `actor`, which gives the same per-driver serialization without a lock. Replace the reflective `getCapability(KClass)` with compile-time-checked optional properties on the protocol (`var glucoseSource: GlucoseSource? { get }`, `var insulinSource: InsulinSource? { get }`, ...) — with compile-time linking there is no reason to keep a type-keyed lookup table, and the `asGlucoseSource()` convenience extensions collapse into those properties. Preserve the exact error-containment matrix: create/initialize failure skips the driver entirely and drops its settings store; onActivated failure leaves the driver inactive and writes no preference; onDeactivated failure still removes it from the active set; shutdown failure still completes cleanup.

Reproduce the activation algorithm exactly: unknown id -> typed error; already-active -> idempotent success with no callbacks; collect conflicts from *persisted* preferences (not the in-memory active map — preferences win on divergence); call onActivated first so the slot is never empty; persist; then deactivate conflicts; then recompute the derived slots. Keep DATA_SYNC as a pure activation tag with no capability interface.

Android's BuildConfig boolean leaves the gated code compiled and testable; a Swift `#if` would remove it from the build and from test coverage. The `@Synchronized` read-modify-write guard becomes registry-actor isolation. Android's `.apply()` loss-on-process-kill edge case is less likely on iOS (the OS flushes defaults on scene suspension), but do not rely on it: write the activation change before returning success from activate/deactivate. `UserDefaults(suiteName: "plugin_settings_<id>")` — a per-driver plist, mirroring Android's per-driver SharedPreferences file exactly. Removal maps to `removePersistentDomain(forName:)`. Android omitted a long accessor, which is the sole reason NightscoutSyncStore string-encodes every timestamp and cursor; there is no compatibility cost to fixing this in a greenfield port. Data protection: these plists default to CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication, which is correct — a driver must be able to persist settings during a background Bluetooth wake on a locked device.

Note one intentional divergence: fanning out to per-subscriber AsyncStreams gives each consumer its own 256-slot buffer rather than one shared buffer, so a slow consumer no longer starves others — strictly better, and it preserves the at-most-once, lossy contract. Fix one Android defect while porting: Android's TextInput persists only on `onFocusChanged` blur, so navigating away without blurring silently loses the edit — in SwiftUI persist on `@FocusState` change AND on `.onDisappear`, which closes the hole. Preserve the store-gating rule (TextInput/Toggle/Slider/Dropdown render only when a settings store exists; ActionButton and InfoText always render — this is how InfoText notes appear on the pump card with no store). Preserve the detail-load state machine: 'Plugin not found', 'No detail available for this card', 'Plugin encountered an error loading detail content', 'Action could not be completed', cancellation rethrown not swallowed. Fix the Android load guard, which only compares cardId and so fails to reload when pluginId changes with the same cardId — key on both.

Distribute as a live value in the driver context that every driver reads and re-reads (never a one-shot snapshot), and republish `SafetyLimitsChanged` from the platform on refresh. Preserve the 1-hour staleness threshold as an exposed signal that the registry deliberately does not act on, and the clear-on-logout reset to defaults. Preserve the milliunits-vs-float-units split (SafetyLimits speaks mU; BolusEvent/BasalReading speak U) and the single 1000x conversion at the Nightscout basal boundary.

ports_cleanly.capability: Nightscout source plugin object (DATA_SYNC-only cloud-mediated driver: metadata, empty initialize/shutdown, onActivated->enable, onDeactivated->disable, InfoText settings descriptor, dashboard card, detail screen, sync_now action)

ports_cleanly.capability: NightscoutSyncEngine (pull, per-connection inclusive cursor, asymmetric-truncation paging, cursor-stall guard, outcome classification)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure Swift over `URLSession` + `Codable` — no platform dependency at all, and it stays unit-testable without a simulator or a background-task harness, which was the whole point of Android extracting it from the worker. ports_cleanly.capability: NightscoutSyncStore (typed persistence over the plugin settings store plus a reactive state value)

Keys carry over unchanged. With an Int64 accessor added to the settings-store protocol, cursors and timestamps stop being string-encoded. Preserve the two behaviors that matter: `recordStatus` must NOT clear the last successful sync timestamp (so the card can legitimately show 'Last sync: <old time>' alongside 'Reconnect needed'), and an unrecognized persisted status string must fall back to NEVER rather than crashing. ports_cleanly.capability: NightscoutDataMapper (ingestion validation, source attribution, cross-source conflict resolution)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure Swift, no platform dependency. Port every bound and every exclusion exactly: glucose 20...500, bolus 0...25 U, basal 0...15 U/hr (= 15_000 mU / 1000); `combo_bolus` stays OUT of BOLUS_TYPES; `correction` is forced to isAutomated = true regardless of the upload's flag; basal activityMode stays blank; every row is stamped source = 'nightscout-source'; the reading's real capture timestamp is stored, never the fetch time (this is what makes a frozen cloud feed age out identically to a frozen BLE feed under the 6-min/15-min freshness policy). One thing that must be made explicit rather than implicit: Android relies on `it.units in 0f..MAX` being false for NaN/Infinity. Swift `ClosedRange.contains` behaves the same way, but write `value.isFinite && (0...max).contains(value)` so the invariant survives any future refactor to `abs()` or optional comparison. Cross-source collision resolution must preserve the asymmetry: CGM and basal upserts keep the FIRST writer (ignore-on-conflict), bolus keeps the LAST writer (replace-on-conflict); unifying them changes which value the patient sees.

ports_cleanly.capability: Nightscout DTOs and backend endpoints (GET /api/integrations/nightscout, GET /api/integrations/nightscout/{id}/data?since&limit, PUT/DELETE /api/settings/plugin-declarations)

ports_cleanly.capability: Plugin declaration sync to backend (bolus category vocabulary PUT/DELETE on active-driver change)

ports_cleanly.capability: Apple Watch surface for this subsystem
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: None required. The watch app must remain a consumer of already-collected data, fed over WatchConnectivity (and optionally its own backend calls), and must not host drivers or perform device pairing. watchOS's lack of custom watch faces and its restricted Core Bluetooth background story therefore do not constrain this subsystem at all (they constrain the Wear-parity subsystem, which owns the `watchface` module).
